subject: MAGA won't let go of their lies

body:
Opponents of voting rights lack the common sense to understand that these anti-voting conspiracy theories are just flat-out lies. They'd rather see a vast web of shadowy interests arrayed against them than reexamine their own values when they lose elections.
That's why they create bills like the SAVE America, SAVE, and MEGA Acts, to strip our fundamental right to vote until only their select few have the privilege to vote.
Step up with $35 or more right now to stop the SAVE Act and defend our right to vote from these vicious attacks >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=080926_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
NYT: Trump Leans on Congress to Address His False Claims of Voter Fraud [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=080926_3&amount=25]
President Trump used his recent State of the Union address and the DHS funding debate to press Congress to advance stalled legislation that purports to address his often-repeated -- and equally debunked -- claims of widespread election fraud. There are stats from the conservative, right-wing Heritage Foundation below that prove it.
The SAVE America Act was fast-tracked by opponents of voting rights and passed the U.S. House of Representatives. Now Trump and his MAGA minions are meeting with U.S. Senators, scheming for ways to get this bill through the Senate ahead of November's midterms.
This bill is a stunning assault on our fundamental right to vote, and we can not afford to let this anti-democratic legislation become law, folks.
PITCH IN $35 RIGHT NOW TO STOP THE SAVE AMERICA ACT NOW ➜ [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=080926_3&amount=35]
Don’t be fooled by the name. This bill would force every voter to present specific types of proof of citizenship to register -- something millions of eligible Americans don’t have on hand. And that’s the point. The bill would also obliterate popular methods of voter registration for all voters, including:
* Registration by mail

* 3rd party voter registration drives

* Online voter registration in states that allow it

* Automatic voter registration
Some estimates say that this bill could disenfranchise up to 11 million eligible Americans , especially women and those who live in under-resourced communities.
“ There’s never been an attack on voting rights out of Congress like this ,” said Alexander Keyssar, a professor of History and Social Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School, and a leading historian of voting rights. “ It’s always been the federal government trying to keep states in check on voting rights, for the most part. ”
Team, the consequences of a bill like this passing would be catastrophic for our democracy. Chip in with $35 or whatever you can today to stop the SAVE AMERICA Act and other voter suppression bills from becoming law >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=080926_3&amount=35]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=080926_3&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=080926_3&amount=25] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=080926_3&amount=50]
GIVE $100 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=080926_3&amount=100] GIVE $250 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=080926_3&amount=250] OTHER AMOUNT [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=080926_3&amount=35]
How do we know non-citizen voting is a made up problem? Because red states and conservative-leaning institutions have spent millions in taxpayer money and donor dollars searching for it and finding minimal results.
For example: The pro-Trump Heritage Foundation -- an organization that has funded anti-voting initiatives for decades -- maintains a database of "election crimes." Their own records only list 24 instances of non-citizens voting in U.S. elections from 2003 to 2023 . In other words -- 20 years of elections, millions of votes, and only 24 alleged non-citizen voters.
Reuters has a fuller accounting in recent reporting. Florida, for example, spent millions investigating voter fraud and creating a new state department to oversee election security. They've only prosecuted two non-citizens for voting since 2022. North Carolina said they found nine non-citizens registered to vote out of 7.7 million voters. Utah recently investigated their entire voter roll of 2.1 million registered voters and found one registered non-citizen who never attempted to vote.
The conservative CATO Institute says it best: " These investigations affirm what is simply common sense. People largely aren’t willing to risk their status in the United States — the land of economic opportunity — for the ability to cast one more vote out of hundreds of thousands or millions in a state and hundreds of millions in the country. "
Team, the lies aren't going to stop, but we can push back and make sure bills like this abomination never pass. Pitch in $35 or however much you can to stand against voter suppression bills in Congress and beyond >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=080926_3&amount=35]

Friend, I hope you’re having a relaxing Sunday evening. I have a very personal note for you. Please, read on.
When I first ran for Congress in 2018, I knew I had a tough task ahead of me. It was Trump’s first term, and my community was reeling from his harmful, extremist agenda. Immigration chaos. The Muslim Ban. Attacks on our healthcare. Cuts to critical programs. The list goes on.
We fought back, we beat MAGA, and we made history.
And in the years since, I’ve had the honor of serving this Minneapolis community and representing the interests of regular folks who usually don’t get a voice in Congress — a place where corporate interests and billionaire donors tend to get the final say.
But now, here we are again. Trump is President, and I probably don’t have to remind you that his agenda is perhaps even more devastating than the first time.
Here in Minneapolis, we watched as I was singled out, then all Somali-Americans were targeted, then ICE descended on our entire state in a blatant attempt to exact political violence on a community that opposes Trump’s rule.
Civil rights were thrown out the window. Homes were broken into without real warrants. Families were separated. Businesses were shuttered. Thousands were thrown into detention camps. Innocent mothers and grandpas were dragged into the street. Little babies, used as “bait” for deportations. Protesters were beaten and abused. Renee Good and Alex Pretti were murdered in cold blood, with Trump’s blessing.
**I’m running for reelection because this struggle is far from over. I’m running for reelection because my community needs a fighter in their corner. I’m running for reelection to make sure something like this never happens again.**
Minneapolis and all of Minnesota has been through so much, but now, on Tuesday, we have our chance to strike back. We have the chance to not only win reelection for this campaign, but to nominate progressive champions up and down the ballot who will fight back against this fascist administration with everything they’ve got.
So, if you’re ready to be part of the movement that takes power back from MAGA and the billionaire class, I’m asking you to join me today with a contribution of any amount.

We just WON our runoff election in Louisiana by a landslide!
This is Jamie Davis, the lifelong family farmer and now the Democrat Nominee running to flip Louisiana’s OPEN US Senate.
We are on the cusp of making history: a Black person has never represented the entire state of Louisiana in the US Senate. But this is our moment. The Miracle on the Mississippi is alive and well.

| | | | | |
# Two Days to Go!
---
| |

Team Berge,
We’re down to the final stretch!
Thank you for every hour you’ve volunteered, every dollar you’ve given, and every way you’ve shown up for Team Berge throughout this campaign. We are so grateful to have you with us.

Monday and Tuesday are our last opportunities to be out across the district before the polls close, and we want Team Berge showing up everywhere we can
---
| |
# Kickin’ It Old School
---
| |

Join us Monday evening and Tuesday morning at busy intersections across the district with rally signs, yard signs, homemade signs, and plenty of energy. Let’s make sure voters see Team Berge everywhere they go!
**Monday:** Roughly 4:15–6:00 p.m.
**Tuesday:** Roughly 7:15–9:00 a.m.
_Times are approximate. Join us for any part of the window!_
**Eau Claire:** Lake St. & Farwell St.
**Stevens Point:** Main St. & Division St.
**La Crosse:** Losey Blvd. & State Rd.
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
---
| |
# Join us on Election Night!
---
|
---
| |
Come celebrate the work this team has accomplished and watch the results come in with Emily, campaign volunteers, supporters, friends, and neighbors. We hope to see you there!
---
| |
# Get Your Network to Vote!
---
| |
One of the most helpful things you can do before Election Day is remind your friends, family, neighbors, and coworkers to make a plan to vote for Emily.
Please reach out to the people in your network and encourage them to vote on Tuesday, August 11. Voters can find their polling place, view a sample ballot, and get personalized voting information at [**www.myvote.wi.gov**](https://us.list-manage.com/19njq3ESiMN?e=1362dd258a&c2id=d51b517ba2e5c823fe0a3e4f0e8330f1).
Every vote and conversation matters!

**This is How You Win an Election**
---
| |
Vern Thompson, candidate for Agriculture Commissioner, has been on the road for months, putting over 12,000 miles on his truck. Vern is out there meeting people where they are—on the farm, at the local café, at town halls and gas stations. He isn’t selling a bill of goods. He is listening to the people. He listens to what is working and what isn’t. He asks about their concerns and their opinions. He is interested in people and takes them seriously. And, guess what? **It is paying off. Big.**
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/1872jmmJWRr?e=37dda778f5&c2id=cdbf6368064ed4acbe3dc3fec7c073dc)
| |
Early on Vern called it: data centers are the electoral issue of 2026. On Thursday night a data center meeting in Mandan drew more that 600 people. Not just Democrats, but people of all political persuasions. 600 people who heard from Vern and local legislative candidates, including Signe Snortland, candidate for North Dakota Senate, the event’s organizer. 600 people who heard Vern call for a statewide moratorium on new data center construction and a ban on non-disclosure agreements for government officials. This isn’t just about [data centers](https://us.list-manage.com/NnoUy0GcqpI?e=37dda778f5&c2id=cdbf6368064ed4acbe3dc3fec7c073dc). It is about the corruption of elected official’s campaigns being paid for by the industries they are supposed to regulate. It’s about farmers paying more and earning less. And school kids sitting hungry in their classrooms while our farmers struggle to find markets for their produce. Vern sees these things and knows North Dakota can do better. And where Is Vern’s incumbent opponent? According to his office, he’s in North Carolina doing who knows what. Vern is on the road taking the pulse of a state that needs elected officials that talk with ordinary folks, not out of state billionaires whose only interest in North Dakota is what they can extract from it.

| | In Bismarck this Tuesday? Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

clean_body: I'm stepping down to give this my all. | | | | Fellow American Patriot, Mike Lindell here, founder of MyPillow and I'm reaching out because this week, I made one of the biggest decisions of my life. After 22 years leading the company I founded, I've stepped down as CEO of MyPillow. I didn't make that decision lightly. For more than two decades, MyPillow has been my life's work. Together, we built a Minnesota company from the ground up, created jobs, and proved that with faith, perseverance, and hard work, incredible things are still possible in this wonderful country. So why would I step away now? Minnesota deserves my complete focus, my full energy, and my undivided attention. I'm all in. 100% -- And today I'm hoping you're all in too. My friend, this decision wasn't about walking away. It's about stepping up for you. Career politicians spend their lives protecting what's best for themselves. They worry about their next title, their next election, and their next opportunity. I'm choosing a different path. I'm putting Minnesota ahead of myself. I'm choosing the fight to save Minnesota and I'm giving it my all. I don't have a backup plan. I'm all in. President Trump honored me with his endorsement because he knows I'll fight for Minnesota without compromise. Now I'm backing up those words and his confidence with action by giving 100% to this campaign. But I can't do it by myself. Every phone call we make... Every yard sign we print... Every door we knock... Every voter we reach... It's only possible because people like you decide this campaign is worth fighting for. If you believe Minnesota deserves a Governor who's willing to sacrifice, willing to lead, and willing to put our state first, I'm asking you to stand with me today. Together, we can save Minnesota. I'm all in. I hope you'll be all in with me. | | | Thank you, and God bless. Mike Lindell, Republican Candidate for Governor | | | | P.S. ---
## Amanda Bell for Congress
---
|
---
#### Two More Days - Here’s How You Can Help!
Hi Everyone! It's me, Stephanie. This is a short one, and don’t worry - Amanda has a message for you too, so read on! We have two days left and with such little time I have two requests for support for Amanda. 1\. Tomorow from Noon to 5pm we are having a blood drive in Oshkosh. We'd love to have you come out and donate and/or volunteer with us for a bit. 1800 Wisconsin Street, Oshkosh, WI 2\. Tomorrow night we are looking for any of you who would like to get together and do a texting and calling bank to get people out to the polls on Tuesday. If you're available for that sometime between 6pm and 8:30pm please respond with your availability. Even if it's just a few minutes, we'd love to have you join us. After these two things, we'll be sitting on the edge of our seats for Tuesday! Don't forget to tell all of your friends and family to get to the polls and Vote for Amanda Bell! Thank you for all you've done so far in this campaign! I appreciate you and look forward to celebrating Amanda's win with you on Tuesday night. -Stephanie Kunkel
---
|
---
#### Upcoming Events
August 10th - Community Blood Drive - Oshkosh August 10th - Virtual Phone Bank - From your house August 11th - VOTE August 11th - Watch Party! Want to host a fundraiser or get to know her gathering in your community after the primary? Send an email to admin@amandabellforcongress.org For more information on any of these events you can visit the Events page on www.amandabellforcongress.org
---
|
---
### From Amanda
By Amanda Bell
Regardless of how Tuesday night shakes out, I am so proud of this campaign. We've accomplished so much in this time together. We raised awareness. We got to meet people who have never had an opportunity to let their voice be heard. We visited so many non-profits and servant leaders in our community. We’ve made some amazing friends and we’ve had a fantastic impact. I am so grateful for all of it. I am grateful for the support. I am grateful for the help. I am grateful for the donations. I am truly honored by the amount of support that people have given me and our community. Our communities are stronger when we all work toward our common goals. Our democracy wins when we ensure people have a voice. So, no matter what happens on Tuesday, lets continue to get involved, do the good work, and show up for our neighbors. I hope you can come out to the watch party on Tuesday night. It’s time to celebrate our hard work! Join us at 7pm at Schmitty’s Oar House in FDL. https://www.facebook.com/share/194qxYDg5u/ Thank you so much for everything. Your determined candidate, Amanda Bell Candidate, Wisconsin’s 6th Congressional District

We have two days left before the general election - When we win on Tuesday we’ll need to get moving on some immediate orders. Box 15, Poynette, WI 53955-0015.

#### Listening Sessions and Fundraisers
Looking for individuals interested in hosting a listening session or fundraiser in their community late august or after. Format: You invite 10-30 friends, family, or associates to your home. Format: Each participant has a chance to voice what’s going well and what is not in current government. Facilitation and format will depend on group size. Each participant has a chance to voice what’s most pressing for them. The candidate will provide an introduction of themselves and respond to any questions from the participants. If you’re interested in hosting a Listening Session please email admin@amandabellforcongress.org for more information.

Friend,

Early voting is almost here and I want to give you a direct update from the ground.
Starting now, Turning Point PAC will be shifting into higher and higher gears every week as we fund the immediate surge of ballot-chasers across America.
This week: **Arizona. Nevada. Michigan. Pennsylvania. Ohio. Indiana. Wisconsin. New Hampshire.**

---|---|---
Paradise Residential Services CEO Jocelyne Ininahazwe and her family enjoyed luxury Mercedes brands while the disabled Mainers who relied on the Medicaid agency for 24/7 care were living in squalor, subject to abuse and neglect by non-English speaking staff, including some who were untrained and never subjected to background checks.
That's the chief takeaway from documents released Friday by the Maine Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS), including a termination letter to Paradise that cited "violations [that] place the health and safety of MaineCare Members in immediate jeopardy."
"[Paradise Residential Services] failed to ensure individuals are protected from abuse, neglect, and exploitation, specifically, lack of food, spoiled food, unsanitary conditions in the home, broken glass throughout basement, individuals have been repeatedly left without staff, staff not supervising or providing services," according to the DHHS letter.
_The Robinson Report_ [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/0e89463b-b71e-4e2c-862c-34cc553b9e15?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) exclusively on Paradise's termination back in March, which came only after the company managed to bilk the taxpayer-funded program for nearly $25 million.
Among the new documents, released in response to our Freedom of Access Act request, is a letter terminating Paradise's provider agreement that describes systemic neglect and abuse of Maine residents, as well as fraudulent billing for residential care that was never provided.
The letter corroborates our earlier reporting, which cited formed two former employees who alleged Paradise was violating disability rights and failing to properly vet employees.
Paradise billed under the state's most expensive Medicaid program, MaineCare Section 21, which provides round-the-clock residential care for adults with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) or Intellectual and Developmental Disorder (IDD).
State officials were told as early as October 2024, by a former employee, of deficiencies at Paradise but failed to effectively protect disabled residents from abuse and neglect until earlier this summer.
Paradise Residential Services, according to a March 6 letter terminating the company's MaineCare provider agreement, was found to have severely violated MaineCare policies during inspections on Dec. 13, 15, 16, 17, 18, and 19, 2025.
The violations uncovered included:
* Failure to maintain clean and sanitary conditions (examples cited: filth with potential to attract rodents; resident incontinence hidden in closets rather than properly cleaned; mold on a washing machine; a member's mother having to train employees on use of the washing machine).
* Failure to ensure access to nutritious food in adequate quantities (examples: freezer containing only half a takeout drink; refrigerator limited to condiments, an uncovered tub of margarine, two foil-covered leftovers, cherry tomatoes, and three desserts, two of which were half-eaten).
* Failure to ensure employees met training and background-check requirements under the College of Direct Supports curriculum and related rules.
* Failures in medication management and secure storage.
* Failures to protect members from abuse, neglect, or exploitation, including repeated instances of members left without staff, broken glass throughout a basement, and inadequate supervision consistent with plans of care.

According to a review of federal Medicaid payment records and interviews with ex-employees, the abuse, neglect, and apparent fraud described by the state were part of a lucrative money-making scheme that led by CEO Ininahazwe and CFO Juste Arakaza, both originally of Burundi.
Ex-employees said in March that Ininahazwe and Arakaza earned handsome salaries while simultaneously paying above-market rent through Paradise to real estate holding companies they controlled.
Secretary of State corporate records show Paradise Residential Services was founded by five investors: Ininahazwe, Arakaza, Tresor Niyongabo, Enock Nijimbere Tshibungu, and Eric Nshimiyimana.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/79654944-6014-494b-b872-105e5453bde6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The crew of "New Mainers" earned a total of $24.6 million from their investment in the residential autism scheme, which ran from 2022 until it was halted earlier this year due to severe deficiencies.
The payment records are even more eye-popping when Paradise's fees are compared to other adult autism providers nationally.
Payment records show the company earned more than $800,000 per year for each of the two-bed residential facilities it controlled, the very facilities the state now says were filth-ridden and hazardous to the well-being of patients. Those residents often paid rent to the company on top of the roughly $33,400 per month the company received per patient from MaineCare.
We have much, much more Medicaid fraud reporting coming. Subscribe to support our work!
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..iXiksoTQGrNQi2SlxUuLlH3U5ycRmZ_Ouo0fFcsUUA4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=210285875)
Federal payment records show Paradise consistently billed more than $32,000 per resident, per month, or roughly $400,000 annually, throughout 2022, 2023, and 2024. The national average for the same exact billing code was flat for all three years at $16,105. That sky-high billing rate places Paradise in the 95th percentile for autism care providers, meaning it was billing more per client than 95 percent of businesses providing the same service.
Paradise Residential Services housed its customers at properties owned by Ninta Services LLC and a trust owned by Ininahazwe.
Real estate records show that shortly after Ninta was formed in 2024, Arakaza transferred properties in Lewiston, Westbrook, and Old Orchard Beach to its ownership. Arakaza also conveyed a Lewiston property to Heaven View Housing LLC in December 2022. Similarly, on Sept. 21, 2023, Jocelyne Ininahazwe conveyed a Gorham property and an Auburn property to the Jocelyne/Jocelyn Revocable Trust for $0 consideration.
As previously reported, the state was alerted to Paradise's noncompliance with employee screening rules in October 2024, but DHHS officials only stopped payments to the company more than a year later.
Ininahazwe was not content with merely running Paradise.
Medicaid records show she also formed Royal Residential Care LLC, another apparent autism company with the same phone number as Paradise. Those same records show that Ininahazwe and Arakaza formed an additional Medicaid agency in Ohio in January 2025, Ebenezer Care Homes LLC.
Ininahazwe and Arakaza weren't the only ones in the Paradise orbit with side hustles.
Kelly-Klaus Sahabo, also rendered Kelly Sahabo or Kelly Shabo, is identified in public reporting and corporate records as the son of Jocelyne Ininahazwe.
On March 9, 2022, the Maine Drug Enforcement Agency (MDEA) arrested him on two counts of Class B trafficking in Schedule W drugs, crack cocaine.
Approximately 76 grams of crack cocaine, with a street value of approximately $7,600, two firearms, one reported stolen, and $3,125 in suspected proceeds were seized from a Buxton residence. Bail was set at $500.
Public records further reflect that Sahabo held a real estate salesperson license, and a consent agreement with the Real Estate Commission followed the arrest.
Sahabo's license later expired or was not renewed in March 2026, the same month in which the Paradise Medicaid scheme came crashing down.
Despite raking in tens of millions of taxpayer dollars to provide care for a vulnerable population, the MaineCare Section 21 industry and its two-bed residential care facilities are subject to little regulatory scrutiny.
Paradise was incorporated in 2020 but never received a license until Jan. 10, 2026, and Paradise is one of many MaineCare agencies that have made millions of dollars on MaineCare Section 21 waiver individuals without a state license.
#### Earning Millions Abusing the Disabled
Maine DHHS found Paradise failed to maintain residences in clean and sanitary condition, citing filth with the potential to attract rodents and mold on a washing machine. The letter states that the mother of one resident had to train Paradise employees on how to operate the machine.
Inspectors found the company failed to ensure residents had access to nutritious food in adequate quantities. In one home, the letter states, the refrigerator held condiments, an uncovered tub of margarine, two foil-covered leftovers, cherry tomatoes, and three desserts, two of them half-eaten.
The lack of food is notable not only because Paradise was receiving more than $33,000 per month to care for the individuals in the home, but also because the residents typically receive food stamp benefits under the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), meaning each should have been able to buy food with their EBT card.
The department found Paradise failed to ensure that employees met state training and background-check requirements for direct support professionals, the workers who provide hands-on care in Section 21 homes. The letter cites two College of Direct Supports audits, conducted in May 2023 and June 2024, and a fiscal 2024-2025 findings summary.
That finding is notable given that a former training director for Paradise said the company hired almost exclusively from the non-English-speaking African migrant population, raising questions as to whether Paradise was billing for "work" provided by individuals who were not authorized to work legally in the U.S.
The department found the company failed to administer medications in accordance with state guidelines, including a requirement that medications be securely stored at all times.
The most serious finding concerns member rights.
The letter states that Paradise failed to ensure residents were protected from abuse, neglect, and exploitation, citing findings that disabled clients were "repeatedly left without staff."
Four residents are identified by redacted name and location, with incident dates ranging from June 2024 to Feb. 3, 2026.
The department cited both the MaineCare Benefits Manual and 14-197 C.M.R. Ch. 1, the state rule establishing the rights of Mainers receiving services for intellectual disability and autism, as the standards Paradise violated.
The sixth violation applies to every resident at every Paradise location: failure to correct previously identified deficiencies and demonstrated inability over time.
The letter's own evidence list shows the department had been documenting problems at Paradise since 2024.
It cites a site visit and feedback to Paradise leadership on Oct. 17, 2024; a Jan. 3, 2025, email to company leadership raising training concerns, noncompliance, and falsification of records; site visits in May 2025; and a house audit in September 2025 with a follow-up report and timelines.
One evidence entry references concerns raised to Paradise leadership by Carol Waig, the company's former training director. Waig said in March that she met in person with three senior state officials in 2025 and handed over a thumb drive of documentation. The senior OADS official at that meeting arrived 10 minutes late, took no notes, and never followed up, Waig said.
The department executed a new MaineCare provider agreement with Paradise on Nov. 17, 2025, according to a copy attached to the termination letter. Paradise CEO Jocelyne Ininahazwe had signed it on June 19. The agreement lists more than 20 waiver service locations.
Inspectors conducted the visits that produced the immediate jeopardy finding beginning Dec. 13, 26 days after the department countersigned the agreement.
OADS notified Paradise of the deficiencies on Dec. 17 and directed the company to correct them and submit a self-assessment, the letter states. Paradise did not correct them, according to the department, and its self-assessment asserted that the deficiencies had not occurred.
The department issued a notice of deficiency with sanctions on Jan. 16, 2026, and suspended authorization for new clients. Additional complaints and site visits followed, the letter states, revealing both uncorrected and additional violations.
The emergency termination came seven weeks later...

State records show Paradise Residential Services, an autism agency run by "New Mainers" from Central Africa, violated disability rights while earning $25 million under MaineCare. | Aug 10 ---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Paradise Residential Services CEO Jocelyne Ininahazwe and her family enjoyed luxury Mercedes brands while the disabled Mainers who relied on the Medicaid agency for 24/7 care were living in squalor, subject to abuse and neglect by non-English speaking staff, including some who were untrained and never subjected to background checks. That's the chief takeaway from documents released Friday by the Maine Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS), including a termination letter to Paradise that cited "violations [that] place the health and safety of MaineCare Members in immediate jeopardy." "[Paradise Residential Services] failed to ensure individuals are protected from abuse, neglect, and exploitation, specifically, lack of food, spoiled food, unsanitary conditions in the home, broken glass throughout basement, individuals have been repeatedly left without staff, staff not supervising or providing services," according to the DHHS letter. The Robinson Report exclusively on Paradise's termination back in March, which came only after the company managed to bilk the taxpayer-funded program for nearly $25 million. Among the new documents, released in response to our Freedom of Access Act request, is a letter terminating Paradise's provider agreement that describes systemic neglect and abuse of Maine residents, as well as fraudulent billing for residential care that was never provided. The letter corroborates our earlier reporting, which cited formed two former employees who alleged Paradise was violating disability rights and failing to properly vet employees. Paradise billed under the state's most expensive Medicaid program, MaineCare Section 21, which provides round-the-clock residential care for adults with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) or Intellectual and Developmental Disorder (IDD). State officials were told as early as October 2024, by a former employee, of deficiencies at Paradise but failed to effectively protect disabled residents from abuse and neglect until earlier this summer. Paradise Residential Services, according to a March 6 letter terminating the company's MaineCare provider agreement, was found to have severely violated MaineCare policies during inspections on Dec. 13, 15, 16, 17, 18, and 19, 2025. The violations uncovered included: Failure to maintain clean and sanitary conditions (examples cited: filth with potential to attract rodents; resident incontinence hidden in closets rather than properly cleaned; mold on a washing machine; a member's mother having to train employees on use of the washing machine). Failure to ensure access to nutritious food in adequate quantities (examples: freezer containing only half a takeout drink; refrigerator limited to condiments, an uncovered tub of margarine, two foil-covered leftovers, cherry tomatoes, and three desserts, two of which were half-eaten). Failure to ensure employees met training and background-check requirements under the College of Direct Supports curriculum and related rules. Failures in medication management and secure storage. * Failures to protect members from abuse, neglect, or exploitation, including repeated instances of members left without staff, broken glass throughout a basement, and inadequate supervision consistent with plans of care. According to a review of federal Medicaid payment records and interviews with ex-employees, the abuse, neglect, and apparent fraud described by the state were part of a lucrative money-making scheme that led by CEO Ininahazwe and CFO Juste Arakaza, both originally of Burundi. Ex-employees said in March that Ininahazwe and Arakaza earned handsome salaries while simultaneously paying above-market rent through Paradise to real estate holding companies they controlled. Secretary of State corporate records show Paradise Residential Services was founded by five investors: Ininahazwe, Arakaza, Tresor Niyongabo, Enock Nijimbere Tshibungu, and Eric Nshimiyimana. | | ---|---|--- The crew of "New Mainers" earned a total of $24.6 million from their investment in the residential autism scheme, which ran from 2022 until it was halted earlier this year due to severe deficiencies. The payment records are even more eye-popping when Paradise's fees are compared to other adult autism providers nationally. Payment records show the company earned more than $800,000 per year for each of the two-bed residential facilities it controlled, the very facilities the state now says were filth-ridden and hazardous to the well-being of patients. Those residents often paid rent to the company on top of the roughly $33,400 per month the company received per patient from MaineCare. We have much, much more Medicaid fraud reporting coming. Subscribe to support our work! Federal payment records show Paradise consistently billed more than $32,000 per resident, per month, or roughly $400,000 annually, throughout 2022, 2023, and 2024. The national average for the same exact billing code was flat for all three years at $16,105. That sky-high billing rate places Paradise in the 95th percentile for autism care providers, meaning it was billing more per client than 95 percent of businesses providing the same service. Paradise Residential Services housed its customers at properties owned by Ninta Services LLC and a trust owned by Ininahazwe. Real estate records show that shortly after Ninta was formed in 2024, Arakaza transferred properties in Lewiston, Westbrook, and Old Orchard Beach to its ownership. Arakaza also conveyed a Lewiston property to Heaven View Housing LLC in December 2022. Similarly, on Sept. 21, 2023, Jocelyne Ininahazwe conveyed a Gorham property and an Auburn property to the Jocelyne/Jocelyn Revocable Trust for $0 consideration. As previously reported, the state was alerted to Paradise's noncompliance with employee screening rules in October 2024, but DHHS officials only stopped payments to the company more than a year later. Ininahazwe was not content with merely running Paradise. Medicaid records show she also formed Royal Residential Care LLC, another apparent autism company with the same phone number as Paradise. Those same records show that Ininahazwe and Arakaza formed an additional Medicaid agency in Ohio in January 2025, Ebenezer Care Homes LLC. Ininahazwe and Arakaza weren't the only ones in the Paradise orbit with side hustles. Kelly-Klaus Sahabo, also rendered Kelly Sahabo or Kelly Shabo, is identified in public reporting and corporate records as the son of Jocelyne Ininahazwe. On March 9, 2022, the Maine Drug Enforcement Agency (MDEA) arrested him on two counts of Class B trafficking in Schedule W drugs, crack cocaine. Approximately 76 grams of crack cocaine, with a street value of approximately $7,600, two firearms, one reported stolen, and $3,125 in suspected proceeds were seized from a Buxton residence. Bail was set at $500. Public records further reflect that Sahabo held a real estate salesperson license, and a consent agreement with the Real Estate Commission followed the arrest. Sahabo's license later expired or was not renewed in March 2026, the same month in which the Paradise Medicaid scheme came crashing down. Despite raking in tens of millions of taxpayer dollars to provide care for a vulnerable population, the MaineCare Section 21 industry and its two-bed residential care facilities are subject to little regulatory scrutiny. Paradise was incorporated in 2020 but never received a license until Jan. 10, 2026, and Paradise is one of many MaineCare agencies that have made millions of dollars on MaineCare Section 21 waiver individuals without a state license. Earning Millions Abusing the Disabled Maine DHHS found Paradise failed to maintain residences in clean and sanitary condition, citing filth with the potential to attract rodents and mold on a washing machine. The letter states that the mother of one resident had to train Paradise employees on how to operate the machine. Inspectors found the company failed to ensure residents had access to nutritious food in adequate quantities. In one home, the letter states, the refrigerator held condiments, an uncovered tub of margarine, two foil-covered leftovers, cherry tomatoes, and three desserts, two of them half-eaten. The lack of food is notable not only because Paradise was receiving more than $33,000 per month to care for the individuals in the home, but also because the residents typically receive food stamp benefits under the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), meaning each should have been able to buy food with their EBT card. The department found Paradise failed to ensure that employees met state training and background-check requirements for direct support professionals, the workers who provide hands-on care in Section 21 homes. The letter cites two College of Direct Supports audits, conducted in May 2023 and June 2024, and a fiscal 2024-2025 findings summary. That finding is notable given that a former training director for Paradise said the company hired almost exclusively from the non-English-speaking African migrant population, raising questions as to whether Paradise was billing for "work" provided by individuals who were not authorized to work legally in the U.S. The department found the company failed to administer medications in accordance with state guidelines, including a requirement that medications be securely stored at all times. The most serious finding concerns member rights. The letter states that Paradise failed to ensure residents were protected from abuse, neglect, and exploitation, citing findings that disabled clients were "repeatedly left without staff." Four residents are identified by redacted name and location, with incident dates ranging from June 2024 to Feb. 3, 2026. The department cited both the MaineCare Benefits Manual and 14-197 C.M.R. Ch. 1, the state rule establishing the rights of Mainers receiving services for intellectual disability and autism, as the standards Paradise violated. The sixth violation applies to every resident at every Paradise location: failure to correct previously identified deficiencies and demonstrated inability over time. The letter's own evidence list shows the department had been documenting problems at Paradise since 2024. It cites a site visit and feedback to Paradise leadership on Oct. 17, 2024; a Jan. 3, 2025, email to company leadership raising training concerns, noncompliance, and falsification of records; site visits in May 2025; and a house audit in September 2025 with a follow-up report and timelines. One evidence entry references concerns raised to Paradise leadership by Carol Waig, the company's former training director. Waig said in March that she met in person with three senior state officials in 2025 and handed over a thumb drive of documentation. The senior OADS official at that meeting arrived 10 minutes late, took no notes, and never followed up, Waig said. The department executed a new MaineCare provider agreement with Paradise on Nov. 17, 2025, according to a copy attached to the termination letter. Paradise CEO Jocelyne Ininahazwe had signed it on June 19. The agreement lists more than 20 waiver service locations. Inspectors conducted the visits that produced the immediate jeopardy finding beginning Dec. 13, 26 days after the department countersigned the agreement. OADS notified Paradise of the deficiencies on Dec. 17 and directed the company to correct them and submit a self-assessment, the letter states. Paradise did not correct them, according to the department, and its self-assessment asserted that the deficiencies had not occurred. The department issued a notice of deficiency with sanctions on Jan. 16, 2026, and suspended authorization for new clients. Additional complaints and site visits followed, the letter states, revealing both uncorrected and additional violations. The emergency termination came seven weeks later... The Democratic Party spent years bringing talented and passionate people into the party. Then it frustrated those people, refused to let their ideas grow, and shut down voices that wanted to push the party somewhere new.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..YLGwzDr4I5U20_0aLiicNI3WU42ViTk2_BcvWpLJjP8?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=210504596)
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..YLGwzDr4I5U20_0aLiicNI3WU42ViTk2_BcvWpLJjP8?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=210504596)
The Democratic Party is seeing this with the Democratic Socialists of America, or the DSA. A lot of people have been in the Democratic Party for many years, even decades, running on certain beliefs, ideas, and policies that have yet to come to fruition.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1477c7a1-0dc7-4147-ae04-f6c9ccdd2680?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So what is the Democratic Party to do? What is this talent left to do?
When you look at how businesses acquire talent, how competition emerges, and how new products get formed, maybe what we are seeing here is the emergence of a new Democratic Party being created from within.
We have seen this play out in business over and over again. Once the need for a product/idea/policy begins to emerge, a company has to make a choice. It can allow a new product/idea/policy to develop from within lead by it's talent. It can let the people behind that product leave and become the competition. Or it can fire the employees, lock the product in the basement, and pretend it never existed.
The Democratic Party is facing that choice with the DSA right now.
Below, I'm playing with an idea about what we can learn from business, how it compares to the modern Democratic Party and the DSA, and what we can expect in the future.
**What do you think about the DSA? What do you think about the relationship between the Democratic Party and the DSA?** ...

A Texas appeals court upheld the [State Fair of Texas' handgun ban](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2u4yAUhVeDOywghOCCYhp3mXZK6xouNhIxFlzHmd0_OVt43SnOj8737zk9IeW0LX_hhY4-sUwbni0jEdYJck4LUKmtrYWAKsZjwRXnSQlluLBcigk8pTdOGrrgZhEG2aGTD2tu9-EhVbe6m5ln4Qdtrdb3IKy3Phrj0Ye7ESHaLrmrTlgppBRS234wQSMioB28mlEzLTAkKrWnFQk_0GL-X95Ye19eXXYr0d7Y7Q9TI1PjeZ59LB99HbkMTI2XZGr8RjnsO0Ju3JejEj_2teTQeCMg5BFS5cux8Rm2rrqwnynn1MyDabG8IOXvIv2W1NupnwAAAP__NeeBGQ) Thursday, ruling that a state law limiting gun bans on public property doesn't reach private groups. The 15th Court of Appeals affirmed a [Dallas County judge's dismissal](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuqzAQRL8GOpC9ELALF6-hy2tvidZ4wZYMjuxNSP7-ivzC7Y400hnN_NznO4YYju0_7mT4vab5oLNEYqY8Y4xhQ065FJ8YOdP63MiTnUHA0AjVSDHjwuFFc4-1M1Y4LWsyclRDd9OjhNqbm-4caOgtSnWzoMWiVCdptNJJR-NYB3PphJJCSiF71erB9USEpPQClvqqF-QCp9yyJ6Y3ljV-0otyu6S9jsYzP0rV_atgqmA6z7P9oE_pSiuYrkEVTI8UA4flQswclkgXFkamZsWQm6-42Z5HY_Fo5AgKAJRuPe-xzsY9zhBjKMNY9WLbMcRvO__1tZeB3wAAAP__v9aCpw) of a lawsuit by Attorney General Ken Paxton and three licensed handgun holders. Dallas owns Fair Park but leases it to the nonprofit fair each fall. Judges found the city didn't create, direct, or enforce the policy. Fair President Mitchell Glieber testified that [no city official helped develop it](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGupCAYBeCnwQ4D6IgWFNvYzbZbmh_4VTaMEPgd5779zUxyn-A2pznJl5Pz777cIcRwbH_hgYZea1oOvGpEIiwLxBg2oFRq3RMBFVzPDXe0ixJq4GLkUizgKDxx6aHxxgo_yQaN1OPQ3SYtVbMbMXXoO73adUC8eYtaD524Oe0653Rnm2DenBilkFLIfmynwfeICDhOTlnsWS_QB0qlpR0JX1DX-JWeWFqXHk00O1GurPvD1MzUfF1Xe1nI75Kp-W0zNYvxJz4Ah5wRYuUunYX4mfcUfeWVgJCvEArfzoNbOHjB_-io8gwvSgd3O8SIx4ZMzU0xPl8hxlAHzXqxPSDEzyb67ZdPo74DAAD__9sNi0Y). The fair banned firearms in 2024 after a man without a carry license [opened fire at the 2023 fair](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGunDAQxvHTmM4rezBgCoo0dC9tSjS2B7DixcieXTa3j3hNDpB2RvpJ_-_X1_KFMcVj-4lPmviz5uWgqyZiprJgSnFDzqXWPTNyofW10U5uAQW9VFZqtaDn-KbFYBMmp8KoG5r0YPu2GwcNzT6hIdNZGIPXhKHz_QBeta0ygxtdp8cmTjenrFZaK23sY-yDISIkO3pwZIRRFCLn8uCdmD5Y1_Qnv6k8fH42adqZzyraHwJmAfN1XY9rRbyfAmYsHH0iAfNdJmBO2WMSMFdGJrliLALmb1X-O8ntdUiHh_xNhzzxw_mQeJ6EqUqfX4VlwJTw9sAOsg1egYcgW90N0vS9kba1JB30rvPKuhBcU6ZwXjGlWPtBGLU9MabvAv7f5d8T_A0AAP__tuyYOQ), wounding three. Chris McNutt of Texas Gun Rights said the policy "does nothing to stop criminals" and turns "peaceable Texans into sitting ducks." Paxton, who argued a government "cannot contract away our rights," can appeal to the Texas Supreme Court.
## Alligators Shot at Fort Worth Refuge
Texas game wardens are offering a [$1,000 reward](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOnDAQhJ8GukW2McYULtLQXdqUaMFrsGTwyewdl7ePuCYP8Her1cxovvnzmB4YUzzW37iT40_I00HXmYiZyoQpxRU5l_PcMiMXCq-VNponJZQBYUGKCReOb5o01t7Nwg-yJid7a9pu6KWqN6csYUfGDh77WXZ6IdX3plOiNWawfqiju-OElUJKIbVtBuM1ESHZYVEz6UoL8pFzaXgjpg-eIf3NbyrNkvc6uY35eVbtr0qNlRqv62pC_ugb5BZUarzPSo1fK6y4E1xYPB0n5BCogBRCQKH7CRiYCrTwHx5uegi5MFy58AYH8qsQLHQwlbo4_7xiSvE0faXFumNM32L800HfTv0LAAD__919jjo) for information on whoever shot three alligators at the Fort Worth Nature Center and Refuge on Lake Worth. Two died between May and July and were left to waste. A nesting female survived with a crossbow bolt in her neck. One animal, a young alligator tagged for a study by [refuge manager Jared Wood](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO4yAYBOCnwR0W_CY2FBTXuMu1V1oYfmwkYiL8J-TefuVt9gG2Hmk03_y7L3eXcjq2v-6Blj6xLAe2MyMR1sXlnDZHpZ7nXshRxfjacMd1AQEjF5pLsThP6Y2Lcl2wqwhGdmjlpMfhZiYJ3W6jWb1fTUQEo8ebGbUa9BRv0SgJ4KBL9qoTWgophVS6N2NQiOhQGw8rKqYEhkSl9rQj4cedMf8vb6y9L48u253oebLhD4OZwdxa64_Vh9iumMF8iRjMuXiXGcwD_3HxC8ZjqcRbqbTzw9GrIvd4EFZesbkaeIkRKwYGsxKjEINmMHfVhmdLOadznJgS28Ol_L2Hfvvj28JXAAAA__-6tYmB), was found floating with a gunshot wound to the head. The other carcass looked like someone had tried to twist the head off the spine. "_It's extremely unfortunate that people would take advantage of doing that to a keystone, protected species on public land_ ," Wood said. Hunting [isn't allowed at the refuge](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO6yAQRb8Gd1iAbWwXFK9xl9duaQ0wtlmREMEkJH-_cpr9gG1ndK_OuV-X9QIhhtv-H65o6LWl9Ya1RCTCvEKMYQdKuZQjEVDG7bHjgXZVQmkuJi7FCo7CE9ceGm-s8LNs0Mhx0t0wj1I1h4FOSjcPoIepd53rxDh6PQxWSdtpZX0TzFknJimkFLKf2ln7HhEBp9kpiz3rBfpAKbd0IOELyhbf6Ym5denaRHMQ3Qvr_jG1MLXUWltny-lx_plaPhGmlvPE1LKlTLymTAf_NeSnIs9YIXuetg0zev79iG9-wjG1NNn4ew0xhqJH1ov9CiF-AOivwz2N-gkAAP__1wqE2g), and alligator hunting elsewhere in Texas runs only during set seasons. ## Mavericks Legend Don Nelson Dies
Don Nelson, the coach who drafted Dirk Nowitzki and [turned the Dallas Mavericks](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHS2yAQhJ9G6s4DCMuooEij7k-bUnOCk2CCwAMXyX77jNPkAf5-d2e_79fX8oUxxbz_xIMsv7ayZLpaImaqC6YUd-RSWwuFkSttf3YKtC5KqBGEASkWdBxPWjT23q7CT7InKx9mHO7TQ6o-2PuGxk96MGJYabsb5_SgaRi1W-mht3sf7WdOGCmkFFKb2zR6TURIZnJqJd1pQT5yqTcOxPTCtqV3OaneXDn6ZAPzs3XDj07NnZqv67odeLajZHqvmNIn1an5wJNqdL8bfBA7NY9Sa92pmUMlAo4HQV4RXEEXoGzAgeBNWAGzh__tRDtlD75kyJRayRCwwRNbIw944RuQAXcCM_bV-ucVU4ptfHRa7AfGf3d6_q7s06q_AQAA__9s5pgE) into a Western Conference power, died Sunday at 86. Nelson took over a Dallas team that had won more than 30 games [only once in the 1990s](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unDAQRp_GdEa2MX-FizR0mzYlGvAYrAx45XFg9-2jvcV9gVt_n46Ozp_H_IBI8dx-w4GuvEKaT7yZsBTMMxDFDUrKzHsqUDKGfxvuuMxGmU6qQWo1w1rihbOFyrtF-VFX6HQ_dE079tpUuwtN13vbroNqlA1NwH5sWwXL2Nmu0W1fRffBqUErrZW2Qz123iIi4DCuZkErrEIfS8p12bHgCzjQO12Y6zUdFbm9lCeL5pcwkzDTfd81x88kzHQuIMx0wIU5rn9ZmCmdHIWZdiCSKcgAB0oPRMDy-ybXBOsut0P6dMoTidMpn8CMLOGGt6yy8887EkXuemHVdkCkL5vy04qXM_8DAAD__zHwiVc). He and his son Donnie hid Nowitzki in a basement before the 1998 draft to keep other teams from getting a look. _"We made a commitment that we were going to draft him,"_ [Nelson said](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGu4yAUheHV4A4LMLZxQTENXaad0rqGaxuJQAR34mT3T8kWXn2kT0f_v9t6g5hiPv7CHS299rJmvFpCIqwrpBQPoFJbOwsBVdz_H3jitiqhJi4Ml2IFT_GJq4Yu2E2ERXZo5WymYVxmqbrTign1YGDWfjQwjxhmIYdhCbMOave4d9F-OGGkkFJIbfplChoRAc3i1YaaaYEhUqk9nUj4grand3li7X25d8meRI_Ghj9MOabcdV09tkf-jEy5vAFTrlGpb6bcypSLgSmnl3EyixmZcqFknjG1knlDX3LgV8w55gMbcV_AnzxvwM_4RXiI2LiZumrD44opxTbNTIvjDjF9D9FvQz6t-gkAAP__VzGJBA). _"He was going to be ours."_ The Mavs traded for Steve Nash that same night, and by 2003, they were winning 60 games. Nelson won five titles as a Celtics player, coached 31 seasons, [won Coach of the Year three times](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOozAQhJ_GdETrxQFcuLjG3X_tlWjBG7Dk2JG9f_jz9ifuFa6ZaUYzo-_P1_JFMcW8_6YnO_l5lCXz2RKLcF0opbiTlNraUYSk8uN754PXBQHHHuZew0KbxDcvhrrgVghWd-z0NI_D3U4au8PZiVlvkzbGgFkBeYPJ8l0P98HC3VIX3VUHswatQZv5ZsdgmJl4thuubJQBDlFKvcnBwj_UHulT3lxvW3l2yR0ir6aGXwq9Qn-e5-27kZRAnyug0Dcp9XP5q1RpCn1eSaG_ZhV6mC-xCn0ouc-cWsl9YJKjzyv1W6HtiHnvE--cg0JvNQ5m0gPApNB31YXXGVOKbZyUgf1JMf17Jv9L9O3wbwAAAP__TciIoQ), and retired in 2010 with 1,335 wins, the most ever at the time. His family said he died surrounded by relatives. A celebration of life is set for Thursday, Aug. 13, at Preston Hollow Presbyterian Church in Dallas.

Peter,
Today, I’m asking you to make your first donation to my Senate campaign in North Carolina. If that’s all you need to hear, you can use this link to chip in:

We all have a part to play in standing up to Donald Trump.

Good morning, Peter.
My name is Adam Kinzinger. You might know me as one of the only Republicans in Congress on the January 6th Committee, and one of 10 Republicans who voted to impeach Trump.
I’ll be straight with you — I’m a proud conservative. But I am going to do what I can to help elect Alex Vindman to the U.S. Senate in Florida this November. Our democracy is more important than parties or politics.
Alex and I are both veterans.
I served this country flying KC-135s and RC-26Bs with multiple tours in Iraq and Afghanistan, and Alex was a 21-year U.S. Army combat veteran who was wounded in Iraq and awarded a Purple Heart.
Both of us took an oath to the Constitution and defended our democracy and fundamental rights with everything we had.
Alex and I may not agree on everything, but I fully trust him to tell the truth, to protect our freedoms, and to work for the best interests of Floridians and all Americans.
But it is going to take all of us doing our part to get him there. And right now, the most important thing you could possibly do to help is making a contribution to his campaign.
So I am asking:
[**Can you please make a contribution to Alex Vindman's campaign for U.S. Senate in Florida? His average online contribution is around $30. Many give more. Some give less. No amount is too small. Hello, I hope you've had a great summer.
Friday brought with it a disastrous jobs report. The economy lost 23,000 jobs in July, well below expectations of a gain of 85,000. That's a difference of 108,000 jobs. June's number was also revised down by 37,000, so you're talking about 145,000 fewer jobs. Perhaps even more ominously, 260,000 more Americans stopped looking for work and left the labor market entirely, as the labor force participation rate dropped to a five-year low. About one-third of working-age-men are now out of the workforce. Inflation is eating up any wage gains.
It's a bleak picture getting worse.
Also this past week, CNBC reported that 63% of Americans now report living paycheck-to-paycheck. That's nearly two-thirds and higher than I've ever seen. 8 in 10 Americans rate the economy poorly.
Costs do seem to be rising everywhere one looks, from the grocery store to the gas pump to the utility bill to the popcorn at the movie theatre. I had a family member visit New York and comment, "Things are more expensive here than they were even last year!" I joke sometimes that the new American motto should be "extracting as much revenue from you as possible." It's a recipe for unchecked family stress.
Not surprisingly, this is showing up in our politics. Abdul El-Sayed won a narrowly contested Senate primary in Michigan last week, a sign of populist anger as he ran against a sensible and productive Congresswoman in Haley Stevens who was endorsed by every establishment Democrat under the sun including the outgoing Senator. Democratic Congressman Shri Thanedar also lost his primary in Michigan, a rarity for an incumbent. It's an anti-incumbency wave.
I understand the anger. Our way of life is getting increasingly shitty and precarious. College grads are coming home to live in the basement instead of heading off to start their careers. The rents are too damn high and houses are unaffordable. Bills go up while your income stays the same. Americans increasingly feel like they can't get a leg up as value disappears into the cloud.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9fc9e1c2-bf22-4958-865d-3ab80805ef71?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I personally think we need Universal Basic Income. And a realignment of the American political system is a necessary step to get there. But change is in the air.
Can the anti-incumbent surge be a positive in some precincts? Last week, the Democratic nominee for the Senate in South Dakota, Julian Beaudoin, dropped out, leaving it as a one-on-one between Independent Brian Bengs and Republican incumbent Mike Rounds. Just a couple weeks before, David Roth, the Dem nominee in Idaho, dropped out to create a one-on-one opportunity for Independent Todd Achilles against 83-year-old Republican incumbent Jim Risch. And today is decision day for Democratic Senate nominee Alani Bankhead in Montana to drop out to clear the way for Independent Seth Bodnar to have a one-on-one vs. handpicked-by-the-incumbent Republican Kurt Alme.
South Dakota, Idaho, and Montana are no one's ideas of battleground states. The Democratic parties in these states are weak and unpopular. Yet an Independent is polling neck-and-neck in all three because, well, people hate the incumbents. The farmers in all three states despise the tariffs. Todd, Brian and Seth are all military veterans with impressive profiles.
Said Todd Achilles, "Most Idahoans are among the working poor, and their costs keep going up the same as the rest of the country."
Anger crosses party lines. I've donated to all 3 of these Senate candidates. Every bit helps and these states are very low-cost and sparsely populated relative to the usual battlegrounds.
Will we see an Independent Senator emerge in Idaho, South Dakota and/or Montana? In a season of anger and 'throw the bums out,' anything is possible. And an Independent Senator or two in a 50-50 or 51-49 Senate could transform politics as we know it. Sometimes, anger looks like military veterans stepping up to serve.

Forty.
That's how many times low-propensity voters need to be contacted before they reliably show up on Election Day.
Not four. Not fourteen. **Forty.**
And contacting voters works best when it comes from a **familiar face.**
A stranger at the door doesn’t move the needle. If we want their vote, we’ve got to send someone they've seen before, someone who knows their name, someone who's already called, texted, or knocked on their door this month.
**[This is why Turning Point PAC's ballot-chasing model is built different.](https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.com/click/e132157/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS90cHBhYy90cHBhY19kb25fc2Jfc2ZfZWxjLWJhY2hwcl9icl8yMDI2MDgwMS8/SZW1haWxfZnJlZXRoaW5rZXJkYWlseV9jb20yNjA4MTA/LbmNsTEU2dW4zaw/qP3V0bV9tZWRpdW09YnImdXRtX3Rlcm09MjMzNzlfZnRkMS0yJmFtb3VudD0xMDA/gannCmg/sbia2464afa)**

---
| | The negotiation that appeared to narrow to a single blockade-for-transit trade on Friday hardened dramatically over the weekend. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said a deal with Oman on new shipping lanes is in its final stages, but stressed that Tehran would not reopen Hormuz unless the US meets several demands. **Iran now requires: compensation for damage from US attacks, an end to sanctions and military threats, removal of the US naval blockade, the release of frozen Iranian assets, and an end to further US aggression.** Brent for October rose about 1% to $84.23; the benchmark now trades roughly 16% above its pre-war level. Dow futures fell 127 points Sunday night on the expanded demands.
---
| | For your portfolio, the expansion from one condition to five is the weekend’s critical development — and it moves in the wrong direction for a quick resolution. On Friday, the deal was a symmetrical trade: US lifts the blockade, Iran reopens Hormuz. **Over the weekend, Iran converted that single trade into a comprehensive list touching sanctions, frozen assets, and war reparations.** For the American investor at or near retirement, this means Brent at $84 rather than the high $70s, which firms the August 14 CPI base case toward 3.8–3.9% and keeps a September rate hike genuinely in play. A near-term signed deal — the scenario that would break Brent below $75 and ease rate pressure — has become less likely, not more.

Sisters and Brothers –
# [](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/46?t=1&akid=50%2E42639%2EqgbE9c)
[](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/28?c0=deluzio-em-jun26.AE9VfX&refcode=em260810&refcode2=50.42639.qgbE9c&t=2&akid=50%2E42639%2EqgbE9c)

Sisters and Brothers –
The political future of our country rests upon one very simple principle: the need for working people to stand together and fight back against corporate greed, and create an economy that works for all of us, and not just billionaires and large corporations.
So when we have progressive candidates with the guts to take on corporate power in this country, we have to do what we can to support them if we are going to have any chance at transforming this country and creating a government that works for all of us.
**One of those people is Congressman Chris Deluzio in Pennsylvania.**
Chris understands that our current healthcare system is broken and wildly expensive. He believes, as I do, that healthcare is a human right, not a privilege, and that we must end the embarrassment of being the only major country on earth that does not guarantee healthcare to every man, woman and child. That is why he supports Medicare for All.
Chris understands that we have a corrupt campaign finance system which allows the very rich and their super PACs to buy and sell politicians. That is why he fights vigorously to end the disastrous Citizens United Supreme Court decision — which allows Big Money to control our political process.
Chris understands that too many workers in America are earning starvation wages. That is why he fights to raise the minimum wage to a living wage, to make it easier for workers to join unions, to build the millions of units of low income and affordable housing this country desperately needs and make sure that seniors can retire with dignity and security.
Sisters and brothers, Chris' campaign is about more than just one single House seat. His work is about taking on the powerful special interests that dominate our economic and political life.

| Peter,
Lately, I've been feeling like the biggest loser...
Why? Because since I started this race, I'm down 70 pounds, and I just won my runoff with 80% of the vote. Those two wins are connected.
This campaign has changed my life and my health. I've been losing pounds by hitting the pavement and knocking doors every day.

And if I'm going to fight for health care against people who think it's a privilege for the rich, I need to be in the best shape of my life.
I may be the biggest loser in pounds this midterm cycle. But the real biggest loser this November? That will be MAGA.
As premiums skyrocket, loved ones are kicked off Medicaid, student loan repayment plans are slashed, and prices for gas, food, insurance, and housing keep skyrocketing, people in every party are ready to send MAGA packing.
I'm Jamie Davis, a third-generation farmer from rural Louisiana who shocked the nation by sweeping my runoff, winning every single parish (what we call counties) in the state, and OUTRAISING MAGA Julia Letlow.
Political analyst James Carville, the "Ragin' Cajun," says Louisiana is in play this midterm. And if I win, I'll be the first Black man elected to this position since Reconstruction.

# DNC WHEN WE COUNT
# 3-Month Progress Update
---
| | **We are excited to share the first**[****](https://us.list-manage.com/CGF9gRWl8_q?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e)[**3-month progress report**](https://us.list-manage.com/GkoD93XMbKu?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e)**for When We Count, the DNC’s national partisan voter registration initiative launched in May 2026.**
The Democratic Party faced a critical voter registration deficit, losing 2.1 million voters between 2020 and 2024 while Republicans gained 2.4 million. When We Count was launched to reverse this trend by training a new generation of organizers to directly recruit and register Democrats nationwide.
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | **OUR IMPACT**
Our youth fellowship pilot in Arizona targeted key congressional districts (AZ-01, AZ-02, and AZ-06) to close critical voter gaps:
**38 Fellows Recruited:** 40% are non-college youth, 38% are Native Spanish speakers, and the average fellow age is 21.
**2,500+ Voters Registered:** 82% registered directly as Democrats.
---
| [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/13bkG2OJ_t2?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e)
| | | | | | | | | | | |
**Reaching Key Communities:** 87% of registered voters are under 35, 58% identify as people of color, and 45% identify as Latino.
**Talent Pipeline:** 7 fellows have already been hired into full-time organizing roles on the Arizona Coordinated Campaign.
---
| |
---
| | **KEY LEARNINGS DRIVING RESULTS**
1. **Rigorous Partisan Training:** Equipping organizers to screen for political preference and openly invite voters to join the Democratic Party drives high partisan registration rates.
2. **Meeting Voters Where They Are:** Targeting high-density gatherings, such as FIFA World Cup watch parties and community college orientations, reaches key unregistered populations.
3. **Sustained Follow-Up:** Early engagement post-registration builds lasting relationships that translate registrations into votes on Election Day.

---
| | **ROAD TO ELECTION DAY & NATIONAL SCALING**
* **Arizona Target:** Expand by hiring +40 new fellows by September 1 to reach 10,000+ new voters registered by the October 5 deadline.
* **National Expansion:** Trained over 1,500 grassroots volunteers across 47 states through a 4-part national training series.
* **Mobilization:** Deployed 80+ voter registration ambassadors across 31 states during the World Cup Final, with two additional national weeks of action scheduled before Election Day.

disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY MIKE LINDELL FOR GOVERNOR**
body:

I'm stepping down to give this my all.
| | | | [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Fellow American Patriot, Mike Lindell here, founder of MyPillow and [_**candidate for Minnesota Governor.**_](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.) I'm reaching out because this week, I made one of the biggest decisions of my life. After 22 years leading the company I founded, I've stepped down as CEO of MyPillow. I didn't make that decision lightly. For more than two decades, MyPillow has been my life's work. Together, we built a Minnesota company from the ground up, created jobs, and proved that with faith, perseverance, and hard work, incredible things are still possible in this wonderful country. So why would I step away now? [**It's simple: because Minnesota deserves a Governor who is 100% committed.**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.) Minnesota deserves my complete focus, my full energy, and my undivided attention. I'm all in. 100% -- And today I'm hoping you're all in too. [**Will you click here to make a generous contribution to my campaign to take back our state and make Minnesota Great Again?**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.) My friend, this decision wasn't about walking away. It's about stepping up for you. Career politicians spend their lives protecting what's best for themselves. They worry about their next title, their next election, and their next opportunity. I'm choosing a different path. I'm putting Minnesota ahead of myself. I'm choosing the fight to save Minnesota and I'm giving it my all. I don't have a backup plan. I'm all in. President Trump honored me with his endorsement because he knows I'll fight for Minnesota without compromise. Now I'm backing up those words and his confidence with action by giving 100% to this campaign. But I can't do it by myself. **[I need grassroots conservatives across Minnesota-and across the country-standing with me.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** _**_Every phone call we make..._**_ _**_Every yard sign we print..._**_ _**_Every door we knock..._**_ _**_Every voter we reach..._**_ It's only possible because people like you decide this campaign is worth fighting for. **If you believe Minnesota deserves a Governor who's willing to sacrifice, willing to lead, and willing to put our state first, I'm asking you to stand with me today.** **[Will you make a contribution of $10, $25, $50, or whatever you can afford to help me win this race?](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** **_Together, we can save Minnesota._** **_I'm all in. I hope you'll be all in with me._**
---
| | | Thank you, and God bless.
---
**Mike Lindell,** _**Republican Candidate for Governor**_
---

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | Hi, I'm Dylan Jovine What a drilling team uncovered deep beneath Utah This unexpected discovery in Beaver County has people saying it could change everything. | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. I just became the Democratic nominee, and I hope you’ll give me a chance to explain why your support today would be so impactful — but if you’re already on board, **[you can click here to split a donation between my campaign and Heartland Patriots to help us kick off our general election campaign.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/107120?refcode=em20260810-10772&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=10772%2E614464%2EeGUggh)**

Today, I see Kansas families hurting under the weight of rising costs and selfish, chaotic leadership from Washington. I’ve spent my life not as a politician, but as a servant — and right now, the best way that I feel I can serve is by running for the U.S. Senate.
