Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Peter,Before I was ever "Senator Collins," I was just a kid from Caribou who grew up in Aroostook County - about as far north as you can go and still call it Maine.Every fall, when the leaves turned and the air got that first bite of cold, I was out in the fields picking potatoes alongside my neighbors. That's how I grew up. That's who I am.You learn things picking potatoes in the County that you can't learn anywhere else. You learn what it means to put in an honest day's work. You learn that nobody owes you anything. You earn it, row by row, bushel by bushel. And you learn to know your way around people who work hard for a living, because you are one of them.That's the Maine I carry with me every single day in Washington. Not the polished version of politics, the real one. The one where you fix the leaky faucet yourself, you know your mail carrier's name, and you never forget where you came from.I've dedicated my life to fighting for the people of Maine - for our fishermen, our farmers, our small businesses, our veterans, our seniors trying to make ends meet. Not because it's easy, and not because it always makes headlines, but because that's what a real Mainer does for other Mainers.I'm still that girl from Aroostook County. And I need your help to keep fighting for the state that raised me.[So, I am humbly asking if you can help me hit my August 15th deadline. We are a little bit behind, and it would mean a lot to get ahead. With Brent back at $84 on Iran’s expanded five-condition demand rather than the high $70s that Friday’s weekly decline had suggested, the July monthly average firms toward a level consistent with a headline near 3.8–3.9%. **The four-day countdown now runs with the energy input tilting slightly hawkish rather than dovish, which firms the case for a genuinely contested September 16 rather than a lean toward a hold.**
---
| | The mechanics matter for your rates. The CPI measures the average price level over all of July, and the first three weeks are locked in. A 3.7% print, which would require Brent to fall sharply in four days on a surprise breakthrough, now looks less likely. Stay balanced but slightly defensive on rate-sensitive holdings.

body:
To help you learn more about Lewis’s works related to Christianity, we produced a powerful, free course

This sponsored message from Inside Scoop Politics is on behalf of Hillsdale College
| | | [](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0U1r3DAQBuBfI99s9GHJ3oMPCc5CIWnpB-QoVGnWHpAlI4037L8vW7bQc64zwzzwvu9v9s1hxLR8dRtMWKsNOdiA1ecrFFrhN7iDbi4FKgetVnJpWj62glvnCa9ge9eESUsxXsYGJjGMRg3ciKFZJ2mMMForf1K96o0xRvRa6VGf-OU0eNfgdP_HR8FFz5XSnZGuFwMHp02QoDXr-bEHR9Bhqhig-pz3PUck9LXLZWnitBLtlaknJs9MnjFdcrdijDW4CB2Eg8nzpQC0vrYRPrC2fi1YCV1CurXhGpg6V8_UzLmU6olzLl7Faf42zy8_mTQHbbbmo3hgat5Lrjt4wrQ8VhsEPDamZtgcxsfQu213uCSmZl_tX9X-r9q7-jjNiSARU_Pzl-fXF_t9aN9__Wj_5dKUKewfGCNWM7CeL3el83lr6LNtXSf5JwAA___4TaVf)
---
| |
Dear Friend,

C.S. Lewis is one of my favorite authors, full stop.

His writings were essential in deepening my faith in God and my understanding of the Bible. Maybe, since you opened my email, he has helped you, too.

Why are Lewis's words so powerful?

It's because he was a master at addressing life's most important questions. His vivid language is delightful and captivating to read.

Lewis's signature ability to communicate the truth about Christianity has inspired so many skeptics to **become** believers and even more Christians to renew and deepen their faith. He is certainly the greatest Christian apologist of the twentieth century.

To help you learn more about Lewis's works related to Christianity, we produced a powerful, free course, "**C.S. Lewis on Christianity** ," which you can now own on DVD absolutely free.

**Claim your FREE DVD set of "C.S. Lewis on Christianity" using this secure link:**

[https://info.hillsdale.edu/free-cs-lewis-christianity-dvd](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0U1r3DAQBuBfI99s9GHJ3oMPCc5CIWnpB-QoVGnWHpAlI4037L8vW7bQc64zwzzwvu9v9s1hxLR8dRtMWKsNOdiA1ecrFFrhN7iDbi4FKgetVnJpWj62glvnCa9ge9eESUsxXsYGJjGMRg3ciKFZJ2mMMForf1K96o0xRvRa6VGf-OU0eNfgdP_HR8FFz5XSnZGuFwMHp02QoDXr-bEHR9Bhqhig-pz3PUck9LXLZWnitBLtlaknJs9MnjFdcrdijDW4CB2Eg8nzpQC0vrYRPrC2fi1YCV1CurXhGpg6V8_UzLmU6olzLl7Faf42zy8_mTQHbbbmo3hgat5Lrjt4wrQ8VhsEPDamZtgcxsfQu213uCSmZl_tX9X-r9q7-jjNiSARU_Pzl-fXF_t9aN9__Wj_5dKUKewfGCNWM7CeL3el83lr6LNtXSf5JwAA___4TaVf)

In this course, you will study Lewis's profound insights on the central topics of Christianity, including:
* Good and evil
* Conversion and faith
* Prayer and the Bible
* Suffering and death
* Heaven and Hell

The instructor, Michael Ward, is a distinguished visiting professor at Hillsdale College and a member of the Faculty of Theology and Religion at the University of Oxford. He wrote _Planet Narnia: The Seven Heavens in the Imagination of C.S. Lewis_ and _After Humanity: A Guide to C.S. Lewis 's The Abolition of Man_. He even spent three years living in Lewis's Oxford home as the resident Warden of The Kilns!

You'll find this course especially moving because it examines C.S. Lewis's beautiful writings about faith. You'll even trace Lewis's own journey from skeptic to believer. The combination provides an opportunity for you to grow in your knowledge and understanding of Christianity.

[So please join us in studying Christianity with C.S. Lewis and Michael Ward with this beautiful free DVD set.](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0U1r3DAQBuBfI99s9GHJ3oMPCc5CIWnpB-QoVGnWHpAlI4037L8vW7bQc64zwzzwvu9v9s1hxLR8dRtMWKsNOdiA1ecrFFrhN7iDbi4FKgetVnJpWj62glvnCa9ge9eESUsxXsYGJjGMRg3ciKFZJ2mMMForf1K96o0xRvRa6VGf-OU0eNfgdP_HR8FFz5XSnZGuFwMHp02QoDXr-bEHR9Bhqhig-pz3PUck9LXLZWnitBLtlaknJs9MnjFdcrdijDW4CB2Eg8nzpQC0vrYRPrC2fi1YCV1CurXhGpg6V8_UzLmU6olzLl7Faf42zy8_mTQHbbbmo3hgat5Lrjt4wrQ8VhsEPDamZtgcxsfQu213uCSmZl_tX9X-r9q7-jjNiSARU_Pzl-fXF_t9aN9__Wj_5dKUKewfGCNWM7CeL3el83lr6LNtXSf5JwAA___4TaVf)

Warm regards,

Bill Gray '01
Vice President
Institutional Advancement
Hillsdale College

**P.S.** You probably know that C.S. Lewis also wrote the children's series, _The Chronicles of Narnia_. My wife and I read those books to our children so many times! I can't tell you how many dog-eared copies we have of these.

One of the best parts of this course is learning how the Christian faith is woven into these captivating stories. **I hope you 'll take advantage of this great FREE DVD offer today:** [https://info.hillsdale.edu/free-cs-lewis-christianity-dvd](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0U1r3DAQBuBfI99s9GHJ3oMPCc5CIWnpB-QoVGnWHpAlI4037L8vW7bQc64zwzzwvu9v9s1hxLR8dRtMWKsNOdiA1ecrFFrhN7iDbi4FKgetVnJpWj62glvnCa9ge9eESUsxXsYGJjGMRg3ciKFZJ2mMMForf1K96o0xRvRa6VGf-OU0eNfgdP_HR8FFz5XSnZGuFwMHp02QoDXr-bEHR9Bhqhig-pz3PUck9LXLZWnitBLtlaknJs9MnjFdcrdijDW4CB2Eg8nzpQC0vrYRPrC2fi1YCV1CurXhGpg6V8_UzLmU6olzLl7Faf42zy8_mTQHbbbmo3hgat5Lrjt4wrQ8VhsEPDamZtgcxsfQu213uCSmZl_tX9X-r9q7-jjNiSARU_Pzl-fXF_t9aN9__Wj_5dKUKewfGCNWM7CeL3el83lr6LNtXSf5JwAA___4TaVf)

NYT: Trump Signs Order Seeking Federal Control of Mail Voting as He Promotes False Claims [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=081026_1&amount=25]
Straight from the New York Times , Team:
" President Trump stepped up efforts to promote his false claims of widespread voting fraud, signing an executive order of questionable constitutionality seeking to create a national list of citizens that would determine voting eligibility and restrict mail ballots. "
Let's be clear: The president has no explicit Constitutional authority over elections, and much of this latest attack on our fundamental right to vote appears difficult to enforce and legally dubious.
This order directs the Department of Homeland Security to create a “ state citizenship list ” based on data from various federal databases. It also directs federal officials to send that made-up list to state election officials, and orders the attorney general to prioritize prosecution of election officials who provide ballots to voters not on the made-up list. It also directs the U.S. Postal Service not to transmit mail-in ballots from any individual not included on Trump's “ state citizenship list ," even though elections are mandated by the constitutional the be run by the states.
This order is yet another sign that the MAGA crew will do anything they can to codify their power permanently and silence the will of the people by suppressing and eliminating the votes we cast.
Our elections are sound and mail-in voting is secure, no matter what Trump says. Step up to defend our fundamental right to vote and the use of mail-in ballots with $35 or whatever you can today >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=081026_1&amount=35]

We all know that mail-in voting laws are about ballot accessibility, making it easier for voters to participate in our elections . It's been used widely in some states for decades and in most of the country since the pandemic.
But that doesn't stop Trump because he's absolutely terrified of what might happen in the next election.
Arizona’s Secretary of State (the official who runs elections), Adrian Fontes, reacted like this: “ The Constitution doesn’t allow the executive to take over elections administration, that’s a job for the state legislatures or Congress, and so I don’t think this is going to pass any sort of judicial muster. He added: “ The greatest threat to American elections is Donald Trump lying about them. ” That''s because Donald Trump’s continued claims about large-scale “cheating” in elections are outright lies.

Felix Hagenimana faces a Bar complaint and Medicaid fraud allegations (Photo: Kiva.com)Another adult autism MaineCare company was terminated in March -- on the same day Gov. Janet Mills attacked Dr. Mehmet Oz's Medicaid fraud crackdown as a political stunt -- according to records released Friday by the Maine Department of Health and Human Services.
Like Paradise Residential Services, Beyond Residential Care (BRC) was run by an African migrant and operated with the massive MaineCare Section 21 program that is designed to provide 24/7 residential care for disabled Mainers.
Both companies are now accused of Medicaid fraud.
But unlike Paradise, BRC was run by an alleged attorney who had his law license suspended following a Maine Board of Overseers of the Bar complaint for misconduct.
The complaint alleges that BRC CEO Felix R. Hagenimana, a Rwandan immigrant who has claimed to have entered the state in 2011, breached ethical requirements via his immigration law firm, Hagenimana Law, PLLC, and Asylum Services, LLC, a Bath-based asylum processing business co-owned with Donald Lader.
The Bar [complaint](https://substack.com/redirect/e1f7e863-c58b-41ce-b9f3-9cfa1912130b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) arrived months after DHHS pulled the plug on Hagenimana's $13.8 million residential autism business, citing inspections that found BRC's disabled residents were neglected and their rights were abused.
Hagenimana, the letter asserts, "shuffled Members between settings to meet the needs of the Provider, not the Members', and not in conformance with Members' needs and choices as reflected in a Person-Centered Service Plan."
At the same time, Hageniamana allegedly took on nearly 1,500 asylum cases over a five year period, a period that coincided with the social services crises in Portland, South Portland, and other major cities, as Maine struggled to cope with the sudden influx of non-English speaking, jobless and homeless migrants from Central Africa.
The high-volume immigration racket involved charging migrants $1,000 to $7,000 to submit asylum claims on their behalf -- claims that, in some instances, were allegedly written using large-language models like ChatGPT.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c939bf8c-2038-4890-b87d-db43252a06fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

The federal records available for BRC are narrower, but they show the scale of the business model in plain English. In the four months where BRC appears in the 2024 federal file for the group-home billing code, the company drew $1.63 million for 48 client-months of care. That works out to $33,905.50 per client per month. At that pace, a single house with two clients would generate $813,732 a year -- roughly twice the $405,000 median sale price for a single-family home in Maine in 2025, according to the Maine Association of Realtors. BRC's billing rate also sits above the national 95th percentile for the same type of group-home, raising questions as to why it took DHHS four years to clamp down on an autism business out-billing 95 percent of its peers. The autism profiteering BRC is accused of fits a model The Robinson Report 's long-running investigation into MaineCare fraud has repeatedly found: rapidly growing Section 21 providers, a small number of disabled clients, very large MaineCare payments, and state oversight that seems to arrive only after the smell of burning paperwork reaches Augusta. It also landed as MaineCare was already buckling. In January 2025, Gov. Mills sought $118 million in additional state funds to close a MaineCare shortfall for the fiscal year, warning that the money was needed to draw down additional federal funds and avoid payment disruptions. Rather than cracking down on MaineCare fraud, Democratic lawmakers passed a series of tax increases to keep the money flowing into businesses like Paradise and BRC. | | | | | [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001rMNvu5BrKp4Mw_XLkozNptwnn5w03tRb7Dakg4iSo_rwtTEjrfiuQE-LFgUwIbFa5K8c_FTccB5PM_E4PcOBakt4dkH4Wt3nCsKlHizZRKZlTnQkxTR19YK2EbYN5pX3aX51XLPj6B4YxG765YB2MbX9Af0lmIqmqCt00YxZ_hZvlfoGzIQyKK_NoiCWH0ITKRLzZUoN5W5to7tUDy5PRVqj6Ow4La5h&c=XAZZYTOpjcev0HeRvWzwrm8qeh9uPE7Rt8vNBbCT1PBdCo4XTcG6UQ==&ch=EaPPJd54ymiakcYs0UAAq0T2kbI8P_T6WZj4-RuH_MUirTGj-ORwFQ==)

| Let me be honest with you about something.
I'm not supposed to be in this race.
The grandson of a sharecropper? Not supposed to be a viable Senate candidate in Louisiana.
A Black farmer from rural Tensas Parish? Not supposed to compete statewide in the Deep South.
Someone without billionaire backers or a Rolodex full of Washington insiders? Not supposed to have a shot at flipping a Senate seat.
But here we are.
And MAGA is absolutely shocked.
They thought Louisiana was locked up. They thought they could focus on defending seats in swing states while the South stayed safely red. They thought a race like ours -- a real populist challenge to their grip on power -- wasn't possible here.
They were wrong.
Look at what's happening: Democrats flipping Trump districts across the South. MAGA candidates tearing each other apart in primaries. Republican retirements at levels not seen since the Great Depression. Trump's approval cratering over his failed Iran war.
This is a once-in-a-lifetime opening. The kind of moment that doesn't come around often in Louisiana politics.
And I believe -- deep in my bones -- that I'm the candidate to meet this moment.
Not because I'm the most polished politician. Not because I've been planning a Senate run my whole career. But because I understand what working Louisianans need because I've lived their struggles.
I know what it's like to watch costs rise while your income stays flat. I know what it's like to compete against corporations that rig the system against family operations. I know what it's like to worry about whether there will be anything left for the next generation.
That's the authentic economic populism that can win here. Not the fake MAGA version that delivers nothing but culture wars -- the real thing that actually fights for working people.
And if we capitalize on this moment -- if we show the political world that Louisiana is genuinely winnable -- everything changes.
Not just for this race. For the entire map. For what's possible in the South.
But only if we have the resources to compete. And that counts on good folks like you stepping up.

Corporate media treats Israel's lobby as the third rail of American politics. **Eli Clifton** and **Ian Lustick** didn't get the memo. This Wednesday, the authors of _Israel's Lobby_ join Drop Site for a live conversation on how campaign cash and political pressure built one of the most powerful lobbying operations in Washington, and why crossing it can end careers. Drop Site's **Ryan Grim** and **Murtaza Hussain** host, and you'll get your questions answered by the group live.
**Wednesday, August 12 at 7:00 PM ET**
This live event is exclusive for our paid subscribers, the people who make this journalism possible in the first place. If you want to support the journalism holding Israel's lobby accountable, and get access to this event and future ones, upgrade today.

**Eli Clifton** is an investigative journalist covering money in politics and U.S. foreign policy, and a cofounder of the Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft. His reporting has appeared in The Guardian, The Nation, The Intercept, Foreign Policy, and elsewhere.
**Ian Lustick** is Professor Emeritus of Political Science at the University of Pennsylvania, where he held the Bess W. Heyman Chair, and has spent decades studying Israeli-Palestinian affairs and American foreign policy in the region.

Fellow American Patriot, Mike Lindell here, founder of MyPillow and [_**candidate for Minnesota Governor.**_](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjR9AAwAAAAAAkF68FilgxRscHLZf-J5v9xqtsC-Kcjl4wr6c8ZOG9ZJlNRc-cp1R8782LffpKPweW8ONVhk_iXGZGo65LZz-DnRbFkJapHp8IjdRAiwjA) I'm reaching out because this week, I made one of the biggest decisions of my life. After 22 years leading the company I founded, I've stepped down as CEO of MyPillow. I didn't make that decision lightly. For more than two decades, MyPillow has been my life's work. Together, we built a Minnesota company from the ground up, created jobs, and proved that with faith, perseverance, and hard work, incredible things are still possible in this wonderful country.So why would I step away now?[**It's simple: because Minnesota deserves a Governor who is 100% committed.** ](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjR9AAwAAAAAAkF68FimopO2tiWKYckAwGhw1bO5R78Be7It03G6nr-oUi6dPUD-NkHvLnOV38B1qrYzeCehk7PlTO5vnJ6NnI0gvB9BwjKs0Ru0W0Yi8w)Minnesota deserves my complete focus, my full energy, and my undivided attention.I'm all in. 100% -- And today I'm hoping you're all in too.[**Will you click here to make a generous contribution to my campaign to take back our state and make Minnesota Great Again?**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjR9AAwAAAAAAkF68FinhnCTCO9S0hPHsL9HMmdauvMta1d9D57KZe_oig8pmngruVnSzVouv-POEu_TKQsAEBt2rp3PRdeDsj-CpdUGH7HK4DHaN-52QA) My friend, this decision wasn't about walking away. It's about stepping up for you. Career politicians spend their lives protecting what's best for themselves. They worry about their next title, their next election, and their next opportunity.I'm choosing a different path. I'm putting Minnesota ahead of myself. I'm choosing the fight to save Minnesota and I'm giving it my all. I don't have a backup plan. I'm all in. President Trump honored me with his endorsement because he knows I'll fight for Minnesota without compromise. Now I'm backing up those words and his confidence with action by giving 100% to this campaign. But I can't do it by myself. **[I need grassroots conservatives across Minnesota-and across the country-standing with me.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjR9AAwAAAAAAkF68Fioe6PBYZTR6UGhN1YVVUdv6bmgilQ7twvZ-ZiUmrCtf91ALQ8UiYl15wFpwhGDQL2yMAqw_3vBYKOiRo0Ldqp74aeqibBjCI_K8g)** _**_Every phone call we make..._**_ _**_Every yard sign we print..._**_ _**_Every door we knock..._**_ _**_Every voter we reach..._**_ It's only possible because people like you decide this campaign is worth fighting for. **If you believe Minnesota deserves a Governor who's willing to sacrifice, willing to lead, and willing to put our state first, I'm asking you to stand with me today.** **[Will you make a contribution of $10, $25, $50, or whatever you can afford to help me win this race?](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NjR9AAwAAAAAAkF68Fip37AyaIhzDfkNYBemMIC-JTOEE3pTpj0qfnMYNzQeK7x3y_6QcndKglTpRsqLeuIYHzAjESCXanJT6VzfvhLG7sOf7NpsUcjY-g)** **_Together, we can save Minnesota._** **_I'm all in. I hope you'll be all in with me._**
---
| | | Thank you, and God bless.
---
**Mike Lindell,** _**Republican Candidate for Governor**_

**Help Shape the Next Session: Your Ideas, Your Feedback**
# Doubling Down on Housing for 2027
For years, housing has been at the top of my agenda, and I've been proud to lead on it. Oregon is in a housing crisis — it's the single biggest cost pressure on the families and businesses I represent — and I've spent my time in the Senate working across the aisle to do something about it. I've reached across party lines and partnered in good faith with Democrats and with the Governor on housing, because this problem is too big and too urgent for politics as usual. But I'll be honest with you: for all the effort and all the bills, we still haven't delivered the results Oregonians need. Homes still aren't getting built fast enough, and prices keep climbing. Now is the time to double down and focus on what we actually know works — the fundamentals that move the needle: more land to build on, fewer regulations standing in the way, and infrastructure that lets our cities grow. Ahead of the 2027 session, my office has been drafting a slate of legislative concepts built around exactly those priorities. These are still draft ideas, and I want to hear from you before they're finalized. Here's a preview of where we're headed. **Freeing up land and cutting red tape.** Too much buildable land is locked up by a slow, litigation-prone system. I'm working on concepts to open supply and get government out of the way where it doesn't belong:
* A one-stop Urban Growth Boundary (UGB) "land swap" process through DLCD, so cities can trade like-for-like property without endless process and lawsuits.
* Suspending SB 100 planning requirements for single-family homes for five years, keeping health and safety rules while dropping parking mandates and design review.
* A building code "sunset" that targets cutting 25% of outdated regulations by 2030, and ends anonymous drive-by code complaints.
* Directing every state agency to prioritize housing production, with the Housing Accountability and Production Office tracking and reporting progress.
* Unlocking infill on already-served land — letting homeowners on unincorporated lots with existing water/sewer split their lot and build, and creating a path for homes on golf-course and other underused parcels.
* A study of Oregon's wetlands to understand how much developable land inside UGBs is being taken off the table so we can remedy and get cities building!

**Lowering the cost to build.** High and unpredictable fees kill the math on the very homes we need most. I'm pursuing concepts to bring those costs down:
* Capping Parks and Recreation system development charges (SDCs) and barring them from funding community centers rather than open space.
* A "starter home" subdivision framework allowing smaller lots and homes with a hard cap on impact/SDC fees so affordable homes actually pencil out.
* Community Development Districts that let growth pay for its own infrastructure over 20 years instead of burdening existing taxpayers.
* Eliminating mandatory affordable-housing percentages on UGB expansions that are stalling projects, and converting LIFT funds from grants back to revolving loans.
* Redirecting state funding into the roads, water, and sewer systems cities need — the infrastructure that unleashes private home builders to build faster and brings down the actual purchase price of homes at every level.

**Growing the workforce and modernizing the rules.** More homes require more workers and smarter housing law. My draft concepts include allowing an accessory dwelling unit (ADU) by right on any residential lot statewide (up to 1,500 sq ft), creating a lower-barrier residential plumbing service-and-repair license to grow the trades, and moving prevailing-wage determinations for affordable projects to Oregon Housing and Community Services. I'm also working on commonsense landlord-tenant fixes — a clearer path to transition employer-provided housing when a job ends, and a new 10-day notice to protect on-site staff from threats and violence. Taken together, these concepts reflect a straightforward philosophy: Oregon can build its way out of this crisis if we remove the barriers, control the costs, and expand the workforce. I'll share more detail as these drafts move through Legislative Counsel, and as always, your feedback shapes the final product. Send us your thoughts and ideas on how we unlock more home ownership in Oregon! sen.dickanderson@oregonlegislature.gov **Senator Dick Anderson**
Oregon State Senate, District 5 |
* * *
---
* * *
---
One of the work groups I'm committed to these days is the Oregon Parks and Recreation Revenue Workgroup—a bipartisan, bicameral group finding creative new ways to move Oregon's parks department forward with a real strategy for success. I'm joined in this effort by Senator Kate Lieber (D), Representative Vikki Breese-Iverson (R), and Representative Emerson Levy (D). (There's a photo of all of us below.) We recently met at Silver Falls State Park for a firsthand look at the challenges, infrastructure, and opportunities that lie ahead for the department.
The work group meets every month through the end of the year. There's a lot to do, but I believe creating incredible parks is part of who we are in Oregon. My office is committed to expanding our parks department to the fullest extent possible. Our parks—which include the entire coastline—are some of the best assets Oregon owns, and we must protect and use these resources for generations to come.
* * *
****
**Working for You in Salem**
Serving the Oregon Coast means showing up wherever coastal voices need to be heard. Beyond my committee assignments in the Legislature, I serve on a wide range of commissions, boards, task forces, and work groups tackling the issues that matter most to our district — from fisheries and ocean science to rural housing, child care, state parks, and support for our tribal communities. Each of these seats is a chance to make sure coastal Oregon has a voice at the table when decisions are made. Below is the full list of where I'm putting in the work on your behalf.
**Coast & Ocean**
* Pacific States Marine Fisheries Commission
* Oregon Ocean Science Trust
* Oregon Coastal Caucus Member
* Blue Economy Task Force

**Children & Families**
* Vice-Chair on Behavioral Health and Early Learning
* Task Force on Liability Insurance for Child Care Providers
* Oregon Child Integrated Dataset Governance Committee

**Tribal Relations**
* Statewide Legislative Commission on Indian Services
* Task Force on Tribal Consultation

**Housing & Economy**
* Vice-Chair Housing and Development Committee
* Senate Committee on Finance and Revenue
* Work Group for Eastern Oregon Rural Housing Needs
* Oregon Life Sciences Competitiveness Task Force
* Oregon Retirement Savings Board (OregonSaves)
* Denmark Industrial Symbiosis Study Tour

**Parks & Culture**
* Oregon State Parks Revenue Workgroup
* Oregon Cultural Trust Board

**Legislative Operations**
* Joint Committee on Legislative Administration
* Joint Emergency Board Subcommittee on Higher Education
* Joint Emergency Board Member and Committee on Ways and Means
* Asset Forfeiture Oversight Advisory Committee

I’ve dedicated my entire career to one
principle: that everyone deserves a fair shot at life.

It’s why I started my career investigating threats to democracy and civil
rights in the U.S. and abroad.

It’s why I became a law clerk in Detroit, fighting to protect and defend
people’s civil rights and freedoms.

It’s why, as Dean of Wayne State University Law School, I worked to ensure
all students could afford their education by freezing tuition and
expanding scholarships.

And it’s why, as Secretary of State, I’ve fought to make everyday life
easier for all Michiganders, secure our elections, and expand voter
access.

But I know our work is far from finished. So now, I’m running for Governor
to make sure Michigan is a place where everyone — from our kids to our
seniors — can stay, grow up, and thrive.

But Michigan is one of the most competitive states on the map this cycle —
and with megadonors like the DeVos family and Elon Musk pouring millions

_**by Cliff Schecter**_
Ohio Republican Congressman Max Miller recorded a video recently to protest his innocence in his alleged and now infamous spousal and potential infant-abuse case.
He would've come off as more believable if he'd just run a black screen with no audio.
This extra-Y-chromosomed whinger--who transmitted vibes of wanting to commit acts of violence against the camera he stared into with the anesthetized eyes of a shark--of course said no abuse took place. Uh huh.
Sadly, this is not just the story of a particular MAGA-humping, bottom-barrel huckster. But part of a web of cruelty, abuse, dishonesty, hypocrisy and lack of accountability that infects any entity when authoritarianism takes hold. So let's back up for a second, and take into account where this took place. Ohio.
But, first, I want to tell you about a very different Ohio, one to which I happily emigrated nearly two decades ago. A true swing state, friends. Really--you can look it up!
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/284efa7d-df9c-4769-a6d2-4f25c8007a89?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I arrived in the heart of it all, as residents of the Buckeye State call Ohio, during the 2008 campaign cycle. My wife grew up here, so this crotchety, cursing-by-the-bushel, New Yorker moved to Cincy to raise my kids and perhaps a little hell in what was then one of the two most crucial states in the country politically. I was recruited by the Ohio Democratic Party to run a secretive opposition research and earned media operation literally out of the basement of party HQ.
God that gig was fun.
The task in front of us: win back 4 swing state house seats and take back a majority for the first time since 1994. We toiled from our banal, bare-walled basement office and visited our candidates in targeted races around the state to share media advice. We worked to find the goods on our opponents to strengthen our messaging. And we injected it into the political bloodstream via creativity and pageantry to drive the message home about Republican proto-Epstein-class corruption, socially-retrograde positions, and basic dickishness.
My happiest moment was watching then Senator Obama win the presidency--in a big way--that night. But I must admit my most personally satisfying was not just securing the four seats we needed to take back the state house, but seven overall. One of which was solely my decision to target, based on the hard-charging candidate, changing demographics in her district, and the Obama-effect.
On election night we won that one by 40 votes. A month later it would be certified after numerous recounts.
_But I 'm sure glad I didn't know then what I know now._
Republicans--with Koch Brothers funds, support from the Forrest Gumps of GOP corruption (they turn up everywhere in history), and Republican House Minority Leader, John Boehner, from Southwest Ohio and badly wanting to be Speaker--made Ohio a key state in which they strategized a sneak attack on the redistricting process. A plan you're now all-too-familiar with, to gerrymander themselves into power. January of that year saw Citizens United pass the oligarch-stenched Supreme Court, and suddenly it was raining men. Or money.
Sorry, I got mixed up with my Lindsey Graham retrospective.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.U-Z17fmwKMYMmS6cIXv0IKcCW1ZgBMHm6aFTi1bLCS8?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=209714747)
So Ohio became one of many one-party protection rackets with a state flag, but pretty much nothing else that resembled a republic. Republicans gerrymandered Ohio so obscenely that the Ohio Supreme Court--with the vote of a Republican Justice-- s _truck down their Statehouse maps five times_ and their congressional maps twice. So what did they do? They made small changes to run out the clock, mostly ignoring the court. In other words, they ran elections still using unconstitutional, rigged maps and kept most of their power anyway.
Sure, democracy in Ohio hasn't technically ceased to exist--you can still put on a charming "I Voted" sticker--but Republicans have worked tirelessly to ensure actual voting rarely threatens their control.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/284efa7d-df9c-4769-a6d2-4f25c8007a89?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This led to the inevitable corruption of a one-party state. There was the FirstEnergy scandal, _which federal prosecutors described as likely the largest bribery and money-laundering scheme ever perpetrated against Ohioan_ s. Roughly $60 million in dark money helped an ass-hat named Larry Householder become speaker and ram through a billion-dollar utility bailout, paid for by--you guessed it--Ohioans! Householder's predecessor, Cliff Rosenberger, resigned after the FBI raided his home and storage unit. Householder's farm was also raided before he was convicted of racketeering and sentenced to 20 years in prison.
**Two consecutive Republican Ohio House speakers had their property searched by the FBI.** Hell, if they can make it three in a row they may even get a free set of steak knives! Seriously, if there were any justice in the world, the Ohio GOP would be forced to replace its elephant logo with a federal search warrant.
And sadly, the rot wasn't confined to bribery and election theft.
This is where we return to the story of Max Miller--which includes, and yes, it is insane--drug abuse, spousal abuse, an online profile of an ostensibly married, Republican "family man" at a gay hook-up site, and donations to all of them by one of Jeffrey Epstein's closest pals implicated in the Epstein files.

Peter,

If you take billions away from public schools, the schools educating Iowa's children will have fewer resources.

That's not a complicated equation, and it's clearly a very bad idea.

**Yet that's exactly what Mariannette Miller-Meeks supports.** Iowa's voucher program funnels taxpayer dollars to private schools, draining resources from the public schools that educate more than 90% of Iowa children.

For rural communities especially, the impact is real. Many schools have already closed, and diverting funding away from public education will only make it harder for schools to provide the opportunities Iowa students deserve.

Christina believes we should be doing the opposite. In Congress, she'll fight to fully fund public education at every level because every child deserves access to a great public school. She won't stop fighting until Iowa is once again the national leader in public education.

Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football’s 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville’s time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year’s Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP’s SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul “Bear” Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. body:

Fellow Arizonan, Socialism has spent years tightening its grip on the Democratic Party, and even a handful of its own members can no longer pretend otherwise. A coalition of House Democrats, led by Reps. Tom Suozzi of New York and Adam Gray of California, published the Promise to America, a [public pledge rejecting socialism](https://us.list-manage.com/oaGRnWY_1NC?e=6477bcd9cd&c2id=f05c70fe8231dcabc26816038b27d5aa) and committing signers to a growing, competitive economy, secure borders, fiscal discipline, and "persuasion over purity." Ten sitting Democratic members of Congress and five candidates put their names on it, but Arizona's Fourth Congressional District's Congressman Greg Stanton did not.The pledge asks for nothing radical of a true moderate, proud American. It simply asks Democrats to say, on the record, what most Americans already assume of their representatives: "We are capitalist, not socialist." "We are responsible with taxpayer dollars." "We reject extremism." For a congressman who has spent seven years branding himself to Arizona as a moderate, this should have been the easiest signature of his career. Instead, Greg Stanton did what he always does:_**nothing.**_ Greg Stanton has been in Washington for seven years and still can't bring himself to put in writing that he does not support the far-left socialist wing of his party. Stanton has had opportunity after opportunity to speak up against this extreme, un-American ideology, and he has proven yet again he stands for absolutely nothing.It fits the pattern of Stanton’s entire career. He has never governed like a man who answers to Arizona’s Fourth Congressional District, because he doesn’t. He votes to stay in good standing with Democratic leadership and keep the special interest dollars flowing, whether it’s in his district’s best interest or not. During his time in Congress, he has introduced 78 bills and resolutions, and only one has become law. He has voted with Democratic leadership on nearly every consequential roll call of his career. He has stayed silent again and again as antisemitism has taken root within his own party's ranks, unwilling to risk the standing he's built with Democratic leadership. And now he is silent on a pledge that simply asks him to reject socialism and affirm American values.Greg Stanton isn't a moderate Democrat. He's an empty suit with Democratic leadership's fingerprints on the strings. He'll tell Arizona he's a pragmatist, but when his own party asks him to actually put that in writing, he goes quiet because he knows a real answer would cost him with the socialists now running his party. Arizona deserves a representative who stands firm in what he believes and speaks out against extremism on either side of the party line. Greg Stanton isn't that man.**WATCH TO LEARN MORE ⬇️**

clean_body: | Fellow Conservative, I'm going to make a prediction... When the votes are counted this November, the radical left is going to be in a state of total shock. And the political establishment is going to spend weeks trying to explain what hit them. But that only happens if Republicans like you are on record before the Midterms. That is how consequential this moment is. But here is the part the pundits won't tell you. None of that happens automatically. The Democrats are at war with the American people -- open borders, defunding ICE, eliminating voter ID, putting men in women's sports. You name it, they are on the wrong side of it. And yet they are running the most radical, well-funded Senate candidates in states across this country who are counting on Republicans to stay home and let them walk right in. I will not let that happen. And I don't think you will either. I made you a prediction at the beginning of this email. I stand by every word of it. But that prediction is built on one assumption -- that Republicans like you are engaged and ready to fight. That is where your assessment comes in. Peter, it's Conrad Cable - the Democrat running to DEFEAT Mike Johnson and send him into political retirement where he belongs.
Let me get straight to it:
Mike Johnson is the head of the MAGA Extremist snake.
Every rotten thing running through this party -- every cut, every lie, every betrayal -- runs straight through him.
He gutted Medicaid. Millions of families lost coverage. He called it "waste, fraud, and abuse." It wasn't. It was grandma's insulin. It was your neighbor's chemo.
He cut SNAP benefits. Families who work full time still can't afford groceries. Mike Johnson looked at hungry kids and decided billionaires needed the tax break more.
He's coming for Social Security next. After a lifetime of paying in, after decades of hard work, Mike Johnson wants to pull the rug out from under every senior in this district.
And when a private company tortured detainees at Winn Correction Center -- choked them, stabbed them with pens, let two of them die -- Mike Johnson said nothing. Not one word.
Mike Johnson will defend abusers all day long. He just won't defend the people they hurt.
Mike Johnson has spent his career striking at the people who can least afford it and calling it leadership. He's not protecting Louisiana's 4th District. He's protecting himself, his donors, and Donald Trump.
I'm Conrad Cable, and I'm done watching this. I'm a farmer. Where I come from, you don't let something poisonous keep spreading through your land -- you deal with it.

#

Friends --
With less than 100 days until the November election, Elon Musk just announced that he’s planning to spend at least **$100 million** to elect MAGA Republicans in the midterms.
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260810-1-b&t=1&akid=11713%2E3935704%2ED_eKSo)
Elon Musk spent nearly $300 million last cycle to help Donald Trump and Republicans return to power. He then spent his time in government gutting jobs to give massive tax cuts to billionaires like himself — while putting thousands of Americans out of work.
Now with the House and Senate majorities back on the line, Elon Musk is trying to buy his way back into power again. We cannot let him.
[**Can you help us make sure Elon Musk’s plans backfire in the best way? Rush in $10 to help GIFFORDS PAC elect gun safety champions everywhere >>**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260810-1-b&t=2&akid=11713%2E3935704%2ED_eKSo &amount=10)
**[CONTRIBUTE NOW](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260810-1-b&t=3&akid=11713%2E3935704%2ED_eKSo)**
We need to take this threat seriously.
Our endorsed candidates like Jon Ossoff, James Talarico, and Roy Cooper could be clobbered by Musk-funded attack ads. If we don’t fight back in time, those attacks could be enough to swing these toss-up races and buy the GOP’s way back into a majority.

# Iran
* **Trump on Iran: "We are low-keying it": **President Donald Trump [signaled](https://substack.com/redirect/61b9f423-d704-469d-9e0a-343a4b499440?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Sunday that he is prepared to let economic pressure on Iran mount rather than launch a new military offensive, telling Axios the U.S. is "low-keying it." "We are only semi-negotiating with them. We are just watching Iran with its huge inflation and the fact they have no money," Trump said.
* Trump also pointed to oil prices falling to slightly above $75 a barrel as easing the war's impact on U.S. consumers. "It will work out. It always works out. It's like a chess game," he said.
* **Iran FM says no current negotiations with U.S., but Oman agreement is close:** Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi [said](https://substack.com/redirect/2f321d8c-8cdb-4a21-ba41-618eeaa30d74?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Sunday that Tehran is not currently negotiating with the U.S., and negotiations would not resume until Washington ends its violations of the memorandum of understanding and compensates Iran for the commitments it breached.
* Araghchi did say, however, that the two sides continue to exchange messages through intermediaries, though he insisted that this is "not called negotiation."
* On Saturday, Araghchi [said](https://substack.com/redirect/3a8a2f6a-7a76-45dd-b413-a152a90b1651?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Iran and Oman are "very close" to an agreement on a new legal and navigational framework for the Strait of Hormuz, stressing again that an agreement with Oman would not fully reopen the Strait.
* **Six demands to open the Strait:** Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, who served until this weekend as Supreme National Security Secretary, [articulated](https://substack.com/redirect/360216be-ff3d-40a0-9863-d1533644b9fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Iran's six demands to reopen the Strait, calling on the U.S. to end all threats to the country, permanently end "war and aggression" against Iran and its allies in Lebanon, Palestine, Yemen and Iraq, lift the U.S. blockade of Iran, remove its naval and air forces from the area, pay for damages caused by its attacks, lift sanctions on Iran, and unconditionally release its frozen assets.
* Iran's terms, Axios noted on Sunday, were the prerequisite for a nuclear deal "until several weeks ago." Now, they are the prerequisite for the Strait reopening.
* **WSJ: Trump hints he will end Iran war with Strait reopening:** U.S. President Donald Trump [told](https://substack.com/redirect/2d9f4429-137b-4b61-9e0a-5aa1b478a0f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) aides he may walk away from the Iran war without a nuclear deal if Tehran fully reopens the Strait of Hormuz, The Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday. Trump said he would lift the blockade if Iran fully reopens the strait, but disputes remain over other demands, including reparations, frozen assets, and waivers for Iranian oil exports, the report says.
* **Vessel struck off the coast of Hormuz** : A vessel was [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/5d854d52-6bfc-470a-a4ad-bfaad9bbea0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Saturday by an unknown projectile near the Strait of Hormuz, 18 nautical miles east of Khasab, Oman, according to UK Maritime Trade Operations. The vessel and crew were reported safe, and there was no environmental damage. Oman's Foreign Ministry [condemned](https://substack.com/redirect/d337ebdf-59e1-4ed1-a626-39bab51394fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) attacks on transiting vessels and warned about their potential to derail its ongoing negotiations with Iran over the Strait.
* **U.S. sneaking millions of barrels of oil through southern Hormuz lane, official tells Axios:** An unnamed U.S. official told Axios on Sunday that "around 8 million barrels of oil are going out of the Gulf every night" through Hormuz's southern lane in coordination with the U.S. military.
* The reporting has not been independently confirmed. Far lower amounts of oil have been [suggested](https://substack.com/redirect/34b23b33-e47f-4b75-be75-84134320bc39?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by available tracking data, with the maritime tracking firm Kpler reporting a total of nearly 16.9 million barrels moving west-to-east through Hormuz from August 1 to August 7.
* **FT: U.S. blockade has halted Iranian exports of crude from Kharg:** Iran's crude exports [appear](https://substack.com/redirect/e884597e-bab2-4e46-a929-27d9ce6accc3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to have stopped due to the renewed U.S. naval blockade, with no tankers loading at Kharg Island for at least a week, the Financial Times reported on Sunday.
* Kharg handles nearly 90% of Iranian crude exports and has been idle since July 31. Iran is still receiving revenue from earlier cargoes reaching Asia, including 26 Iranian-flagged tankers near Malaysia, but that income could dry up within weeks under a blockade. Empty tankers are also unable to return, while storage levels indicate Iran has begun cutting production, the report noted.

* **Vance says the U.S. is still "in the middle of the game" in war with Iran: **In a Sunday interview with Fox News, U.S. Vice President JD Vance [said](https://substack.com/redirect/c9329543-7557-40ab-b5d4-602548fcbca3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the U.S. characterized the war with Iran as not presently near a resolution, saying that the U.S. was "in the middle of the game," and that it intends to leverage its economic, military, and diplomatic advantages to "get the best outcome for the American people."
* Vance said the administration's immediate priority is "getting as much oil and gas out of the Middle East" as possible.
* He said Washington expects Gulf exports to return to prewar levels once the Strait reopens under a new agreement. He also claimed that Iran had told the U.S. it will neither impose tolls nor fire on commercial vessels, and that Iran is "hurting" and looking to get out of the conflict.
* **Pentagon orders U.S. defense companies to speed up weapons production:** The Pentagon [issued](https://substack.com/redirect/2ab81b38-da19-4191-9561-adf3d1481850?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a memo on Wednesday ordering U.S. defense companies to dramatically speed up the production and delivery of weapons and ammunition, as the five-month war with Iran depletes American arsenals.
* In the memo, Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg gave contractors a maximum of 21 days to submit plans to "drive significantly faster, more aggressive delivery schedules" for critical weapons.
* The U.S. has burned through much of its stockpile of long-range precision missiles in the war. The Post reported the military fired more than 850 Tomahawk cruise missiles in the first month of the conflict alone, faster than manufacturers can replace them, alarming some Pentagon officials.

* **Mohsen Rezaei appointed to lead Iran 's Supreme National Security Council:** Iran named former Revolutionary Guard commander Mohsen Rezaei as head of its Supreme National Security Council, according to state media. Rezaei replaces Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr, who was appointed after Ali Larijani was killed by an Israeli strike in March.

# Yemen
* **Saudi and Saudi-backed forces shell areas in Saada and Taiz:** Four civilians, including two children and two women, were [wounded](https://substack.com/redirect/2104e339-927e-47e6-a7ce-87e80e4f2151?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) when artillery from Saudi-backed forces struck a home in Wadi Hansh in Taiz, Yemen on Saturday, according to an Ansarallah media official. Separately, Saudi artillery shelled Tabara village in Ghamr district of Saada governorate, Al-Masirah reported.
* Ansarallah-aligned governors in Hodeidah and Lahj urged residents to reject recruitment by Saudi-backed forces, warning them against becoming "fuel for the Saudi war."
* **Yemen 's UAE-backed Southern Armed Forces claim drone strikes on Ansarallah:** The Emirates-backed southern Armed forces [said](https://substack.com/redirect/ec4bb59e-d90e-4fc1-9933-ff937775be32?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Saturday they struck Ansarallah positions across three fronts in northern Dhale governorate. The Southern Armed Forces claimed "heavy losses" in personnel and equipment but provided no casualty figures.

* **Fires reported at two major Saudi Aramco energy sites:** Two fires were [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/5aee7a0c-b2b3-4d26-9505-f4d4f98d521f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at two Saudi Aramco sites on Saturday.
* Satellite fire-monitoring data showed a major thermal event at the Berri Gas Plant near Jubail on the Gulf coast. The extent of damage and cause remain unclear.
* Separately, Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry confirmed that a fire broke out at dawn at a facility belonging to Aramco's Jizan refinery on the Red Sea coast. Aramco crews extinguished the blaze and no injuries were reported. Ansarallah claimed the attack.
* **Ansarallah launches assault on Red Sea port, killing seven:** Ansarallah [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/0019de49-177a-41b1-8548-285ab72421bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the government-held Red Sea port of Al-Mokha on Yemen's western coast with ballistic missiles and drones on Sunday. The "National Resistance Forces," aligned with Yemen's Saudi-backed government, claimed four troops and three civilians were killed and 30 wounded, with a pier, buildings, and stored food damaged.
* **Oman works to contain oil spill near protected marine reserve:** Omani authorities are [working](https://substack.com/redirect/b236afe6-a478-4c42-bb77-81bb9dd15d09?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to contain an oil spill covering around 390 square kilometers near the Hallaniyat Islands, more than a month after the tanker Caroline Bezengi, carrying roughly one million barrels of Russian oil, ran aground in waters off the country's southern coast, according to Oman's state news. The spill threatens environmentally sensitive areas, including coral reefs, turtle nesting grounds, and marine habitats around the Hallaniyat Islands marine reserve.
* The cause of the incident has not been determined, though British maritime security firm Vanguard previously reported explosions aboard the tanker off Yemen's Mukalla coast on June 6 that caused flooding and disabled its main engines.

# Palestine
* **Netanyahu formally rejects U.S.-backed Gaza roadmap:** Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu formally [rejected](https://substack.com/redirect/53ffa870-e2a6-47bf-b40d-077f6917aabc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a U.S.-backed 15-point Gaza roadmap announced by President Trump at the end of July, saying Israeli forces would not withdraw until Hamas was "fully disarmed" of heavy and light weapons.
* He said Israeli forces would [continue](https://substack.com/redirect/235f9bef-4dd1-444a-af45-55f7521962d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) military "operations" in Gaza against what Israel labels "threats" to its forces and civilians.
* Netanyahu also ruled out a Palestinian state in either the occupied West Bank or Gaza.
* "Unlike all those who lecture us, we do what needs to be done for Israel's security, and we can and know how to stand our ground, even against our best friends when necessary," Netanyahu said, in a reference to the U.S.
* Last week, Israeli ministers and security chiefs [discussed](https://substack.com/redirect/6eb302a8-e43d-4bab-a29e-3b7a8ffd0f74?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) resuming attacks on Gaza to signal that Israel rejects the U.S.-backed 15-point phase 2 roadmap accepted by Hamas, according to the Times of Israel. The report follows a lull in Israeli airstrikes over the past several days, though shootings by Israeli troops have continued, killing and wounding Palestinians. During the meeting, one minister reportedly described the roadmap as a "diplomatic October 7."
* **Hamas reaffirms commitment to 15-point plan:** Hamas [said](https://substack.com/redirect/50af3545-56bd-4a6e-80e5-e5197e4ec0e6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a Sunday statement that it remains committed to the 15-point Gaza roadmap agreed upon with mediators and supervised by the U.S.
* It reiterated that its priorities are an end to Israeli attacks, Israel's withdrawal from the Strip, the reopening of crossings and the entry of aid and shelter materials.
* Senior Hamas official Basem Naim [said](https://substack.com/redirect/356539af-7ca3-45cd-8dea-3b2b75251e97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) about the group's position that it "expects the mediators and the American guarantor to pressure Netanyahu and his government to adhere to the roadmap and not obstruct the process for internal political and electoral reasons."
* **Mladenov defends Israel, claims no troops beyond Yellow Line:** Nickolay Mladenov, High Representative of the Gaza Board of Peace, [said](https://substack.com/redirect/f7a4b8dc-b65f-48e1-8cc1-18ae71a586ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Sunday that Israeli forces would begin a phased withdrawal only after all weapons in every sector of Gaza--including heavy, light, police, and personal arms--are surrendered and "rendered unusable," contradicting the plan originally released by the Board and agreed to by Hamas. The plan includes a parallel process of storage of "heavy weapons" by the Palestinian resistance alongside a phased withdrawal by Israel.
* "Nobody is required to do anything, last of all Israel," before this happens and is verified, he said. In the same remarks, Mladenov falsely claimed that, "currently," Israel had no "beyond the Yellow Line." The original demarcation left Israel controlling roughly 52% of Gaza. Israeli officials now say forces control around 70%.
* **Killed and wounded in Gaza:** Over the past 24 hours, six Palestinians were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,386 killed, with 174,256 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,258 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,145, while 807 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble.
* **Israeli attacks kill 13-year-old girl, wound several Palestinians across Gaza:** A 13-year-old Palestinian girl was [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/e642da31-ad7c-458f-b530-2efb2ceef8e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday after succumbing to wounds sustained when Israeli forces shot her on Saturday in the Al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis, southern Gaza, WAFA reported. Several Palestinians were also wounded by Israeli fire in Jabalia, northern Gaza, early Monday, while Israeli artillery shelled multiple areas across Khan Younis, Al-Bureij, and Beit Lahia.
* **Israeli attacks on Gaza over the weekend:**
* Israeli forces [shot and wounded](https://substack.com/redirect/46994dbc-c67f-413c-abd9-88a7a1c201e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) three Palestinians in Khan Younis on Saturday morning, according to WAFA.
* Israeli forces shot and [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/56e2f85d-11c0-4639-a1e7-f760e3053083?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a young Palestinian man near Deir al-Balah in central Gaza on Saturday.
* On Sunday, Israel [shelled](https://substack.com/redirect/493ebf49-5e6f-4fb6-97a4-a27d0b238227?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Al-Bureij and Jabalia refugee camps, Israeli tanks fired on Gaza City, and the Israeli navy bombarded the coast near Al-Bureij, Khan Younis, Rafah, and Gaza City.
* Israel [shot and wounded](https://substack.com/redirect/c7d8556b-d3cf-4905-82bf-51dcd0e125bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) three more Palestinians, including a child, on Sunday evening, opening fire in the central Khan Younis neighborhood of Al-Najjar and the western Al-Dahra neighborhood, according to WAFA.
* **Israeli attacks in the occupied West Bank:**
* **Nablus:** An Israeli settler attack on the town of Beit Furik, east of Nablus, [injured](https://substack.com/redirect/5d20490f-6c51-4572-b54e-e8833557ef74?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two Palestinian men on Saturday, WAFA reported. Israeli soldiers [shot and wounded](https://substack.com/redirect/d6a8c8d2-5588-4008-bade-a0ef954dfbd7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) another Palestinian youth on Monday morning during a raid on the Balata refugee camp, detaining five others.
* **Jenin:** Israeli forces [stormed](https://substack.com/redirect/164eb450-f7cf-405a-ab1b-c02d0f4a1f02?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the town of Ja'bad, in the Jenin governorate, on Saturday, sealing off its entrance and raiding dozens of homes, detaining several Palestinians in the process, according to WAFA. Israeli forces [began](https://substack.com/redirect/2342db57-1bbd-49bb-a3d8-bfea91890c39?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) bulldozing Monday Palestinian land between Marka and Qabatiya, south of Jenin, to establish a military post and build a settlement road. Forces also seized agricultural land and bulldozed the surrounding area.
* **Hebron:** Israeli settlers [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/a9d24a68-e611-4d0b-a96a-497694344160?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Palestinians in a mosque in the town of Idhna on Saturday, an assault for which Israeli soldiers provided cover. During the attack, soldiers detained seven Palestinians, including the imam of the mosque. A separate settler attack in Wadi al-Rakhim on Saturday evening [injured](https://substack.com/redirect/03bdd837-b4d3-4550-92e4-92479fd3c49b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) six Palestinians, one of whom was shot, according to WAFA. On Sunday, Israeli forces [opened fire](https://substack.com/redirect/09229c6c-2542-4b94-ad67-1c1d29f3d004?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on a shepherd while he was grazing his flock in Idhna, killing three sheep and injuring several others.
* **Bethlehem:** Israeli forces [deployed](https://substack.com/redirect/36ecbe45-38c4-40d6-8385-d19db9dcc62e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) sound bombs and tear gas canisters during a raid on the Dheihesh camp on Saturday evening, inducing several cases of suffocation, WAFA reported. * **Ramallah:** Israeli forces [fired](https://substack.com/redirect/d2c24d24-24ef-430b-ba1a-0a6cd2b0952f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) tear gas into a Palestinian home during a Saturday evening raid in al-Mughayyir, leaving several members of the family, including children, struggling to breathe. * On Monday, Israeli forces [detained](https://substack.com/redirect/dab8e616-a19d-41f7-9ae0-382b49188e4c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Mahmoud Shalato, a former Palestinian detainee from the town of Aboud after raiding his home and ransacking its contents. * **Al Aqsa mosque stormed again:** As many as 133 Israelis illegally [stormed](https://substack.com/redirect/86e5ae0c-29a5-405b-b2bf-d96426a9f6a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Al-Aqsa mosque on Sunday under the protection of Israeli police, WAFA reported.
