| |
### FROM REP. RYAN CHAMBERLIN
---
| |
Most people don't realize they don't actually own their home.

Even after you pay it off — the government keeps a permanent lien on it. Miss the yearly bill, and you find out real fast who really owns the property.

I sat down for an interview on Florida property tax relief and answered the questions everyone's afraid to ask:

\- Why property tax is the **only** tax in America on money you've never made
\- Where the money really went when property taxes jumped 50% in just 4 years
\- How we replace the revenue **without** raising taxes on residents (hint: 143 million people are already using services you're paying for)
\- What actually happens to police and fire if we do this

The answers surprised even the person interviewing me.

*[*](https://us.list-manage.com/hFnXV1n174F?e=d1c1b9864f&c2id=d3808649044f505f0f4143aac3cd50ac&m=68iUSKA3yv0Lo3KFVx9d9sdPN2iux8sYKH5CaZQBu3SQ3RlRADZGechmdmw=)[](https://us.list-manage.com/wqGjV6h4Dry?e=d1c1b9864f&c2id=d3808649044f505f0f4143aac3cd50ac&m=cT4zWt_yZgpPDNaPbgAUNq3EUgPXBFNjO2UYQXWkQ9UFztojqkG_QswfvpY=)[ Watch the full conversation here:** ](https://us.list-manage.com/VcKv7TfYA9x?e=d1c1b9864f&c2id=d3808649044f505f0f4143aac3cd50ac&m=TxSDeRYxNSxvM7zs7P8Nw55OtXTJv_NccWvHpdmVvWfGNFot9NQwlLvfHVE=)

name: Dan Rayfield
subject: We’re taking on Donald Trump—and winning
body:
| | |
---
| | Peter**—**

It's been a busy eighteen months as Attorney General, and I wanted you to get this update directly from me. We're making great progress on the things that matter most to Oregonians... despite everything that Donald Trump is throwing at us.

**A year and a half in, we've now taken Trump to court nearly 70 times. And we've protected $6.9 billion in federal funding for critical services that Oregon families depend on. **

We fought President trump's illegal tariffs, which increased costs for families and businesses**—****and won**. Even as Trump keeps trying to find new ways to raise costs for working families, we're continuing to fight him every step of the way.

But that's just one example. **We'll never hesitate to stand up for Oregon and the people who call it home.** When prices skyrocket for families and small businesses due to corporate greed and illegal mergers, we're there doing the job the federal government refuses to do by tackling the affordability crisis for working families.

When pharmaceutical companies conspire to drive up the cost of prescription drugs, we'll be in court holding them accountable. And when Trump comes after critical services that families need, we'll be there to block him.

**The work ahead is just as important.** While Election Day is a long way off, we have seen what happens to the people that stand up to Trump and his billionaire class. They have literally billions to spend. We need to be ready.

We'd love to have your support. Please consider [making a contribution](https://us.list-manage.com/vpxyv76gWz7?e=1768325bd4&c2id=0fcd3a526fabf816bd24466788989260) today to help us get an early start and keep fighting for Oregon values.

If you'd like to get involved in another way, I'd love to hear from you.
Please reply to this email if you're interested in supporting my campaign, hosting a house party, or attending an upcoming event. Your support**—** whether through a contribution, opening your home, or simply showing up**—** will make a real difference.

**Thank you for standing with me. I'm grateful to have you in my corner. **

Sincerely,

Dan

clean_body: | | | | | Peter— It's been a busy eighteen months as Attorney General, and I wanted you to get this update directly from me. We're making great progress on the things that matter most to Oregonians... despite everything that Donald Trump is throwing at us. A year and a half in, we've now taken Trump to court nearly 70 times. And we've protected $6.9 billion in federal funding for critical services that Oregon families depend on. We fought President trump's illegal tariffs, which increased costs for families and businesses—and won. Even as Trump keeps trying to find new ways to raise costs for working families, we're continuing to fight him every step of the way. But that's just one example. We'll never hesitate to stand up for Oregon and the people who call it home. When prices skyrocket for families and small businesses due to corporate greed and illegal mergers, we're there doing the job the federal government refuses to do by tackling the affordability crisis for working families. When pharmaceutical companies conspire to drive up the cost of prescription drugs, we'll be in court holding them accountable. And when Trump comes after critical services that families need, we'll be there to block him. The work ahead is just as important. While Election Day is a long way off, we have seen what happens to the people that stand up to Trump and his billionaire class. They have literally billions to spend. We need to be ready. We'd love to have your support. Please consider today to help us get an early start and keep fighting for Oregon values. If you'd like to get involved in another way, I'd love to hear from you. Please reply to this email if you're interested in supporting my campaign, hosting a house party, or attending an upcoming event. body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=241003%2E444211%2EY6l7Qg)
Another surprise victory in Tarrant County!
You may know that Tarrant, home to Fort Worth and Arlington, is often called “the last reliably Red urban county in America.”
That may have been the case years ago, but today Tarrant is both a battleground and a bellwether for the rest of the state.
I became the first Democrat in decades to win it in 2018, and since then it has see-sawed between the parties.
Afraid of permanently losing power, Tarrant Republicans have used their control of the County Commissioners Court to try to reduce Democratic voting power.
**First,** they gerrymandered County Commissioner Alisa Simmons out of her district last year, hoping to silence her voice and the votes of her constituents.
**Then, when Simmons fought back by running for County Judge, Republicans proposed to close nearly half of all voting locations in this county of more than two million people.** You can probably guess that a significant number of those proposed closures were in Black and Hispanic neighborhoods.
Well, last Tuesday, during the Commissioners Court meeting that was set to ratify the polling place closures, **Alisa’s leadership inspired so many Tarrant County residents to come out in protest that the Republican majority on the Court were shamed into retreat.**
[](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260810.IOoQjG&refcode=ema20260810-241003&t=3&akid=241003%2E444211%2EY6l7Qg)
They voted to postpone the issue to their September meeting, where we hope it will be put to rest once and for all.
[](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260810.IOoQjG&refcode=ema20260810-241003&t=4&akid=241003%2E444211%2EY6l7Qg)
This is a critically important victory for democracy and for Democrats in what I consider to be one of the most important counties in the state.
It’s another shocker on top of Taylor Rehmet’s stunning victory in a special election in Tarrant earlier this year, where he defeated the Republican candidate for State Senate by 14 points — the same district that Donald Trump won in 2024 by 17 points!
[](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260810.IOoQjG&refcode=ema20260810-241003&t=5&akid=241003%2E444211%2EY6l7Qg)
And to put a cherry on it, James Talarico just held a rally in Tarrant where more than 1,300 people came out to cheer him on in this “reliably Red county.”
[](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260810.IOoQjG&refcode=ema20260810-241003&t=6&akid=241003%2E444211%2EY6l7Qg)
Something exciting is happening in Texas.
It’s thanks to great leaders like Alisa, Taylor and James. And it’s thanks to amazing Texans like our Powered by People volunteers who helped power Taylor’s victory in January... are out there right now registering new Democratic voters in Tarrant to ensure Alisa is the next County Judge... and volunteering to make sure every person at James’ rallies is registered and ready to vote.
[**Please help us build on these exciting victories by donating today. Your support gives our team the resources we need to make the most of this moment!**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260810.IOoQjG&refcode=ema20260810-241003&t=7&akid=241003%2E444211%2EY6l7Qg)
**[Donate $3](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260810.IOoQjG&refcode=ema20260810-241003&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=26&akid=241003%2E444211%2EY6l7Qg)**
Thank you,
Beto

subject: A story of faith lost, tested, and found again
body:
| | | |
---
| | | Patriot,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

body:
Data centers are driving up your electric bill and eating up farmland. Shapiro rolled out the red carpet.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/UsjekYJDCK_?e=63ab67bb25&c2id=8377c90e3583a614e646f5b9492ea9fd)
| | | | | | Peter,
Something is happening across Pennsylvania that you need to know about.Massive data centers — built to power artificial intelligence for some of the biggest corporations in the world — are consuming enormous amounts of electricity and driving up energy costs for everyone. They’re being built on farmland. And they’re being welcomed in by Josh Shapiro.
**Until it became a political problem.**
For months, Shapiro rolled out the red carpet for data center developers. He celebrated their investments. He posed for the press releases. Then, when Pennsylvanians started seeing the impact on their electric bills and their communities, he suddenly changed his tune and started criticizing the very projects he helped attract.
Here’s what’s actually happening:
⚡ Energy auctions are hitting price caps because data centers are consuming so much power that the grid can’t keep up
💸 The cost is being passed directly to you — residential ratepayers are subsidizing big tech’s electricity consumption
🌾 Data centers are being built on productive farmland instead of industrial or brownfield sites
🏘️ Local communities had no say in whether these facilities would be built in their backyards
Stacy Garrity has been consistent from the start. And today, we’re putting our full plan on the table.
---
| [MORE INFO](https://us.list-manage.com/oJCKaTikfwB?e=63ab67bb25&c2id=8377c90e3583a614e646f5b9492ea9fd)
---
| | Our 5 Steps to Get Data Centers Right:
1️⃣ **Pause future development:** Give local communities the opportunity to understand the impacts, ask questions, and provide input before another shovel hits the ground
2️⃣ **Require data centers to bring their own energy and water:** No more sticking ratepayers and communities with the bill
3️⃣ **Prioritize brownfields:** Build on industrial and brownfield sites, not productive farmland. Limit problems in neighborhoods and increase land value
4️⃣ **Give local residents the final say:** The people who live in the community should determine its future, not Harrisburg politicians and out-of-state developers

Cliff sat down with Nikki Fried--chair of the Florida Democratic Party, and the last Democrat elected statewide--for a special edition of AMPED UP. Watch the whole thing. It earns every one of its thirty-three minutes.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.jlbUWxFrgRQtrzayccS9hiLjGHEzhpBBbzJJWbf9zTg?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=210631723)
Five moments to watch for:
* **2:55 -- Thirty years of receipts. **Fried has known Ashley Moody since 1996--college, law school, the Florida cabinet. Then she tells you what happened to $10 million in kids' Medicaid money, and who signed off.
* **9:30 -- The $87 million porta-potties.** A real number from Alligator Alcatraz's no-bid contracts. Cliff asks the only reasonable question: Do they fly?
* **14:20 -- Hoarding is a disorder.** Except, apparently, when it's billions. The robber barons built libraries; these guys shoot Teslas into space.
* **19:25 -- The number that should terrify Florida Republicans.** More doors knocked since March than the entire 2022 cycle--and Donald Trump is now represented by a Democrat.
* **28:45 -- "To not be the last statewide Democrat."** Fried's mission, her answer on whether Key West can be saved, and the bar she's naming after all of this.

Hit play. Then send it to a friend in Florida--[primaries are Tuesday, August 18, and FloridaDems.org is where to plug in](https://substack.com/redirect/d5207384-b370-4a64-8e0b-8753283957e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

Friend, it’s
Justin J. Pearson.

When Tennessee Republicans passed new, unfair, racist maps designed to
eliminate TN-09 as the state’s only majority-Black, Democratic district —
they thought that would be the end of our Movement.

They couldn’t have been more wrong.

We’re still here. We’re still mobilizing our People and communities. And
we’re still building something the far-right can’t buy and can’t take away
from us.

That’s truly powerful,
friend. But
now our campaign is entering a new chapter — one that’s going to test us
in different ways than anything we’ve faced so far. As we continue forging
ahead, I’m hoping I can count on your support.

authoritarian power grab.

After the Supreme Court gave the green light, Donald Trump and his
extremist allies have been eager to push racist redistricting schemes —
across the South, state by state, district by district, so they can choose
their voters instead of letting voters choose their leaders.

And Republicans have eagerly backed this effort. Why? It’s simple: when
more People can freely and fairly participate in our democracy,
Republicans risk losing their grip on power.

That’s why they’re redistricting now — well before voters get to have a
say in November.

I won’t sugarcoat it — we have our work cut out for us. The new TN-09 is

who have come to do us harm.

I’ve done my homework: Retaking our majorities will be a close contest. We need to gain four seats to take back the Senate, which means we need to put up a strong defense in Michigan and Georgia, AND a strong offense in Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, and Alaska.
**But I know Democrats can win if we have the resources to put up a fight. That’s why I made the decision to contribute over $1 million this year to invest in these states and 17 others.**

clean_body: Your support in July meant so much. Thank you. Your support in July meant so much. Thank you. | | | | | | | Peter, Thank you for your strong support in July. We want to be honest with you about what July looked like from our perspective. Sabato's Crystal Ball moved 14 races toward Democrats in a single update, but Texas Senate stayed put. Polling continues to show this race is neck and neck. One Silicon Valley billionaire wrote a $10 million check to James Talarico's super PAC. Democrats raised over $1.1 billion nationally in the first six months of this year alone. Everything was moving in the wrong direction. And then the conservative grassroots did what conservatives do. You showed up. You gave. You proved that this race is not going to be decided by billionaire checkbooks and coastal money. July was the strongest grassroots fundraising month of this entire campaign, and it happened in the middle of the worst national environment Republicans have faced in years. That is not a small thing. That is the difference between a campaign that can compete on television through November and one that cannot. If you were able to give,THANK YOU. If you weren't able, we hope you will While July was great, we cannot stop here. James Talarico still has a significant financial advantage. The national wave is still building. And we have less than 100 days until Election Day. July proved that Ken Paxton has the grassroots support to win this race. August is where we show that it was not a fluke. If you were part of our best month ever, thank you again. Thank you! | | Dear David, Iʼve got to admit, before this campaign started, Iʼd never attended a house party. I mean, Iʼd been to parties in houses before, but that special campaign event where a bunch of super politically active neighbors gather in someoneʼs living room to hear from a candidate for higher office? That was new to me. But after I attended the first house party of my campaign at the home of my dear friends, Joel and Laura, I knew that this political tradition was going to be key to our campaignʼs success. Over the past year, I’ve made house parties a central part of our campaign. There’s nothing like standing in a room full of neighbors, taking questions, and having face-to-face conversations about our future. Last week, we had a terrific house party in Newmarket at the home of my friends and supporters, Ranan and Suki. **We also had a special guest: C-SPAN!** [](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/gemfqQAZOc9cWJCDMWX_fg~~/AAUS1hA~/MHzm2paYuqqpr-Xoo4O5pDJ85-NaAFd362xPAkW24w4Yd63lzxmkH5LOBX3Mi1My7HiqALJ2bgT01MI-zXenLe68MJj6lL2cQxt-WB3fgwB5izhq3YvD84Dv_q-u2CLlhUL06qs7xAW45AhiqVF8Mosoy-0w_F-I2TJpVjKzT1CoU6uUpjEkmHnrzEGfBoGAEygJF8pm8wagGyVFoJ_QNgBMmHDVCZPIbG1rtEUZxLeqeN0YQRLD-oLlKUmuPj1o4tcvq-S6qzUvqtvQeybXwA~~) I know that’s probably not what you were expecting, David. No, itʼs not CNN or MSNOW... itʼs better! Who doesnʼt love the raw, lightly edited stream of fresh news that C-SPAN serves up on a 24-hour loop!? **Having the national press in the room proves that our campaign is gaining traction.** There’s _no way_ C-SPAN would’ve shown up to one of our campaign events a year ago. I know you probably have a LOT of emails from Democrats hounding you for money. I get my fair share too, so I know how annoying it gets. The reality is that U.S. Senate candidates like me rely on small-dollar fundraising to build the resources we need to win. When folks chip in a buck or two at a time, it makes a bigger impact than you may realize. **I hate sending you so many messages, but I want you to know that I don’t take your support for granted.** When I do ask you to pitch in, it’s because I’m up against an urgent deadline — and TOMORROW is Election Day. Peter, Social Security has kept countless Americans out of poverty, but its future under Trump and a corrupt Supreme Court is uncertain. We have an opportunity to expand and protect Social Security, _but we must act now._ Rep. John Larson (D-CT) just released an updated version of his landmark bill to expand Social Security: _The Social Security 2100 Act._ **If enacted, this bill would fulfill the promise of our Social Security system, extend the lifespan of the Social Security trust fund, and reduce inequality.** **[We can’t miss this chance to expand Social Security and keep millions of Americans out of poverty. Become a grassroots co-sponsor of this bill today, and demand your representative pass The Social Security 2100 Act!](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3-fYoCOM0GhPtGWT4ibJudeUoPVA3-GKSvaWOPx5pQKwlplrROCD9Y-etFTeurFKA-XN1ftQAVhBd7GS10iSwt-L9CgvF0qO_gg9kn4ZfBWFqgN_Q-c6aV8wZdfMo_ynDefsONbyWavGWZm3kh-0Zqthowihf2-EkjzZNSF9PKlDJhBArM-2AcE4eFw5ISySmAfh1fTswpoUrhqjiVELMW6GCvjt_in-lvAocJGxcE-Ib-hI3M4rThEd6RQ3Rkt7J9E6X5tyxRnmQeLS2t9cGshvkVTUULs01_1pUrCqasrfpJvk1ijOi-SeDdh0bNwrFlUN1jF0Shfn1qiyfiBxhrsLh-oUKdG8vNgIr1cp7V03nJyyvx4DbD7IRbJjvFuR33rXWHa3_WgnF_B0ZzeP-Z-5Zvp9JkVH-3VlkbqXvlJXKHtP6r6X7Q1VdPNSU_4bbDNDQIXdnyz5ty9StIwrhMeiDPZkwdZPZcMQ7dV0xQIGA/4t2/jBePVFptTXei3sG6odpt2g/h0/h001.FacMPoKu_XRRORBLf15Qjqn_o6I4cA6QA8a7N4nWJFo)** If passed, The Social Security 2100 Act would extend the lifespan of the Social Security trust fund, increase benefits for all beneficiaries, vastly improve cost-of-living adjustments, and more. The bill would also reverse some of the damage caused by the Trump administration by undoing SSA staffing cuts, blocking future attempts to close field offices, and preventing ‘DOGE’ and others from accessing sensitive information. **As history warns us, with our Supreme Court held hostage by dark money, it’s crucial that we expand and protect Social Security**** _now._** This Friday marks the 91st anniversary of Social Security becoming law. After it passed, it was nearly declared unconstitutional by that era’s hyper-conservative Supreme Court, which struck down New Deal reforms like a judicial game of Whack-a-Mole. The program was narrowly saved only by FDR’s bold threat to pack the court. **Our Supreme court now is the most conservative since 1937, and it’s not a stretch to think it has Social Security in its crosshairs.** As one law scholar put it, “don’t underestimate how much a Court remade in Trump’s image could dismantle. Even Social Security could be on the chopping block.”[1] **We need leaders with the same courage as FDR to fight to keep this program alive, and who will not just maintain the status quo on Social Security, but protect and expand it to its full promise.** As FDR himself said when he signed Social Security into law, the program was _“a cornerstone in a structure which is being built but is by no means complete.”_[2] For millions of Americans, Social Security is all that stands between them and poverty. We must protect it at all costs– _and demand that Congress expand and complete the work we started nearly 100 years ago._ **Congress has the power to expand Social Security, and we have the responsibility to make sure they do. Congress needs to pass this bill**** _now,_****before it’s too late.** **[Tell Congress that it’s time to keep building Social Security. Become a grassroots co-sponsor of The Social Security 2100 Act today!](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm3-fYoCOM0GhPtGWT4ibJudeUoPVA3-GKSvaWOPx5pQKwlplrROCD9Y-etFTeurFKA-XN1ftQAVhBd7GS10iSwt-L9CgvF0qO_gg9kn4ZfBWFqgN_Q-c6aV8wZdfMo_ynDefsONbyWavGWZm3kh-0Zqthowihf2-EkjzZNSF9PKlDJhBArM-2AcE4eFw5ISySmAfh1fTswpoUrhqjiVELMW6GCvjt_in-lvAocJGxcE-Ib-hI3M4rThEd6RQ3Rkt7J-jM1hDhlWhT0TknzC6kS0FbwmPUOkcpVYtjVGPb9nSmFUehJBNPr3jyVOyRO4yugh-5gHxHtLFW0eP4FBsWrBzOUz_LvwznOGyNYGNcYNHhdXG6qbs7xXWbGvv-cUncyf4U_cq-Ohl-D01V0VbYkaWKFHvJn4Q-mj-4djb0aZpBwewD_l0NM0dNn2iIvU079B3htJVPjxgE-fsxlfR29mUCrR8Ac32GBaQAzekc9Q-yw/4t2/jBePVFptTXei3sG6odpt2g/h1/h001.Lj7EtJpLUuUUyOC_sSJMLv1oW--N4Ewmr6IkckmaAZw)** In Solidarity,

body:

Peter,
The primaries are finally behind us. Now the real work begins.
Congratulations to all of our Democratic nominees who won Thursday, and thank you to everyone who stepped up to serve their community and state. Special thanks to every volunteer, donor, organizer, and supporter who made our statewide Democratic momentum possible.
While we have a strong gubernatorial candidate, we are still facing the possibility of a Marsha Blackburn governorship. Fortunately, there is reason for optimism. Last Thursday, 403,482 Republican primary voters chose someone other than Marsha Blackburn, joining 353,660 Democratic voters who want something better for Tennessee. While not all of those anti-Marsha Republicans will support Democrats in November, we know there are hundreds of thousands of Tennesseans across the political spectrum who prefer a different path forward.
A vote for a Democratic Tennessee House candidate is a vote to stop Marsha Blackburn. Breaking the Republican supermajority would be the strongest check on Marsha’s extremist agenda and the best way to protect all Tennessee families.
As of today, we have real opportunities to flip seats in Knox, Shelby, and Montgomery counties while defending key Democratic districts across the state. More counties may join the list. Last week's results proved that when we recruit strong candidates, invest in our campaigns, and organize our communities, Democrats can win.

**Maryland is not a safe blue state.** Two of the last four governors before me were Republicans. Just four years ago, we had a Republican governor.
**That means one simple thing: We can’t give this race anything less than our all.** **[If you’re with me, will you rush a contribution to our re-election campaign right now?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260810-2.WojEVB&refcode=em-20260810-2&t=2&akid=1723%2E1086043%2E4gFGWv)**

My opponent Dan Cox is a MAGA extremist who backed the effort to overturn the 2020 election. He wants to hand this state back to Trump on a silver platter.

**[We cannot let Maryland turn red. Can you chip in $5 or any amount today to make sure that doesn’t happen?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260810-2.WojEVB&refcode=em-20260810-2&t=4&akid=1723%2E1086043%2E4gFGWv)**

Here in Texas, that gap is stark enough that many talented people choose a different career instead. I spent three years teaching middle schoolers before I went on to earn my PhD. I know what a good teacher gives a classroom, and I know how much our communities stand to lose every time low pay pushes one out the door. This isn't inevitable. It's a choice. The same choice Governor Abbott made with his voucher scam, and the same choice this administration makes every time it treats federal education funding as expendable. Pay isn't keeping up with the high cost of living, especially for new teachers just starting out. Here in Texas, that gap is stark enough that many talented people choose a different career instead. I spent three years teaching middle schoolers before I went on to earn my PhD. body:
Peter, I filled out my annual financial disclosure form in less than a minute – because I don’t own any stocks.

That’s a good thing. It means that – unlike Republicans – I’m not abusing my office to get rich off trading stocks.

When I first ran for Congress, I drove for Uber to make ends meet, took on credit card debt to pay the bills, and got denied from apartments because of my credit.

I’m still not rich, and I’m proud of that.

Think about it: shouldn't we have more leaders who know what it’s like to struggle? I think if we did, Congress would work a hell of a lot better than it does now.

Forty.
That's how many times low-propensity voters need to be contacted before they reliably show up on Election Day.
Not four. Not fourteen. **Forty.**
And contacting voters works best when it comes from a **familiar face.**
A stranger at the door doesn’t move the needle. If we want their vote, we’ve got to send someone they've seen before, someone who knows their name, someone who's already called, texted, or knocked on their door this month.
**[This is why Turning Point PAC's ballot-chasing model is built different.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e12215357/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS90cHBhYy90cHBhY19kb25fc2Jfc2ZfZWxjLWJhY2hwcl9icl8yMDI2MDgwMS8/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA4MTA/LbmNsMFpyUzNNZQ/qP3V0bV9tZWRpdW09YnImdXRtX3Rlcm09MjMzNzlfd3IzJmFtb3VudD0xMDA/ganpQwg/scm6d5769c1)**

[FINANCE AND TRAIN A BALLOT CHASER](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e12215357/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS90cHBhYy90cHBhY19kb25fc2Jfc2ZfZWxjLWJhY2hwcl9icl8yMDI2MDgwMS8/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA4MTA/LbmNsMFpyUzNNZQ/qP3V0bV9tZWRpdW09YnImdXRtX3Rlcm09MjMzNzlfd3IzJmFtb3VudD0xMDA/ganpQwg/scm6d5769c1)

We don't parachute volunteers in for a weekend blitz and call it a “ground game.”
Turning Point PAC embeds **trained, full-time ballot-chasers** in targeted precincts — the _same_ chasers, the _same_ doors, the _same_ voters — building real relationships week after week until their ballots are in the box.
That sustained presence is what low-propensity voters respond to (and how Charlie delivered all 5 swing states for President Trump in 2024).
**But turnout takes money**. That’s especially true in a midterm election where there’s no “Top of the ticket” generating natural enthusiasm and turnout. History shows many conservatives don’t vote in midterms unless someone makes them.
Early voting starts in less than 8 weeks. And the margin of our House majority — the margin that protects everything President Trump has built — will be decided by whether our people show up or stay home.
Forty contacts. A familiar face. Financed and sustained through November 3.
**That's the formula.[Your contribution DIRECTLY funds it.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e12215357/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS90cHBhYy90cHBhY19kb25fc2Jfc2ZfZWxjLWJhY2hwcl9icl8yMDI2MDgwMS8/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA4MTA/LbmNsMFpyUzNNZQ/qP3V0bV9tZWRpdW09YnImdXRtX3Rlcm09MjMzNzlfd3IzJmFtb3VudD0xMDA/ganpQwg/scm6d5769c1)**

[PUT A FAMILIAR FACE ON CONSERVATIVE DOORS](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e12215357/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS90cHBhYy90cHBhY19kb25fc2Jfc2ZfZWxjLWJhY2hwcl9icl8yMDI2MDgwMS8/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA4MTA/LbmNsMFpyUzNNZQ/qP3V0bV9tZWRpdW09YnImdXRtX3Rlcm09MjMzNzlfd3IzJmFtb3VudD0xMDA/ganpQwg/scm6d5769c1)

Turnout doesn't happen by accident.
It's financed. Contact by contact. Knock by knock. Face by face.
Help us save America.
For Charlie,

**Tyler Bowyer**

name: Chris Brooks, LCV
subject: Bill McKibben, today's clean energy, and optimism
body:
To view this mail in a browser, copy https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTM4NzgzMjUS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjUyMDAzNDIyMQS2&mt=1&rt=0 into your browser.
Peter, did you catch Ezra Klein’s recent podcast about clean energy https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/w_ywTKRk3AJk/Y0luWWE2VjhSNXByZDVBbTZGNlhubjQydFA3M0lYVTBGaFF2MUNkK3dWNmRPQ0E1YmFXc1pFTFNLYjl6R243QTlWbDFHTUJMdC80T1loNHM5U2FtV3hVQ2x2akRRYjFMcTAwU2NGS21oeGs9S0/? The episode features a powerful conversation with Bill McKibben,the longtime
climate activist, environmental scholar, and founder of 350.org and Third Act. McKibben spoke about the incredible progress that’s been made on clean energy
technology. Solar and wind technology have advanced to a point where he
describes them as “the Costco of energy. Cheap, available on the shelf, in bulk, ready to go.”In fact, Australia has deployed so much solar power that during the sunniest
hours of the day, electricity is free. Hearing this made me both excited and frustrated. While Americans' energy bills
are skyrocketing, other countries have figured out how to offer free
electricity! But I still land on optimism, because the only thing standing in
our way is the political will to make the clean energy transition happen here at
home. Weeks later, this quote from the conversation has still stuck with me: “We’re not short of energy, but we are short of time. If we’re going to make any
sort of real difference in the single most critical question that humans
face, then we have to do this very fast. Faster than economic forces by
themselves would produce.” That’s where you and I come in. We need to do this together, and we need to do
this fast. LCV can help us get there. LCV builds power to influence policy and hold our
leaders accountable so that we can develop the political will necessary to make the clean energy transition —
before it’s too late. Thanks so much for supporting this work. Our future depends on it. Best, Chris Brooks

Vice President, Membership
League of Conservation Voters This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Thanks for your support.

clean_body: | | Kids deserve stronger protections online — and parents deserve the peace of mind that comes with knowing their children are safe. That’s why Josh is leading bipartisan efforts to close dangerous loopholes that allow underage users to access age-restricted platforms. Josh’s Facial Recognition to Protect Children Act would require sportsbooks and prediction markets to verify a user’s age with a visual check before allowing anyone to place a bet, helping prevent minors from accessing these platforms in the first place. This is the kind of practical, bipartisan work Josh is focused on every day. If we’re going to keep building support for these efforts, we need a strong grassroots team behind him. = | | = For too long, online platforms have relied on the honor system when it comes to age verification — and kids are paying the price. Simple safeguards aren’t enough when children can bypass them by using someone else’s account. = | = — Team Gottheimer | Josh Gottheimer represents New Jersey’s Fifth Congressional District. Peter, I’ll be honest with you. The way the midterms are going to be conducted keeps me up at night. I worry that Trump and the Republicans will do anything they can — _anything_ — to cheat and try to rig the election in their favor. We’ve seen the gerrymanders, designed to wash out the true will of the American people. We’re witnessing an administration increasingly desperate to enact new voter suppression tactics — whether it’s costly and unnecessary ID laws or threatening to deploy ICE to the polls in certain communities. I fear that they’ll find an excuse to declare an emergency of some sort to justify the use of troops. But I know we can still win. Eighteen months ago, some of the anti-democracy machinations we are witnessing today would have seemed fanciful. We might have said, _“No way that is going to happen”_ — but now, to be frank, we don’t have the luxury of hoping for the best. We have to fight for it. [**We’ve seen what Republicans are willing to do to gain an unearned advantage, and we have to be prepared for the worst. Americans fought to end slavery when its end once seemed impossible. Women fought for the right to vote. Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr., Diane Nash, John Lewis, and countless others understood the power of ordinary people to organize, to stand up, and to move this country forward.
Progress happens because the people fight for it.
That is what gives me hope now. But the fact that we have power is not, in and of itself, enough. **We have to use it.[Please make a donation today to help build the grassroots power necessary to meet this moment.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136993404/639281336/1548394306?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_HolderUpAtNight_email_20260810-NDRC-Tier1-HolderUpAtNight_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260810-NDRC-Tier1-HolderUpAtNight_&utm_campaign=HolderUpAtNight&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImQzMmM3NjA2LTBiOTUtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMGQzYTExZmEzMCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=SAJQ7eMPejbNM8pbGsqVJS_YFmsHi6UlcUFjluEGUd8=)**

clean_body: The GOP are capable of anything - we have to stop them | Peter, I’ll be honest with you. The way the midterms are going to be conducted keeps me up at night. I worry that Trump and the Republicans will do anything they can — anything — to cheat and try to rig the election in their favor. We’ve seen the gerrymanders, designed to wash out the true will of the American people. We’re witnessing an administration increasingly desperate to enact new voter suppression tactics — whether it’s costly and unnecessary ID laws or threatening to deploy ICE to the polls in certain communities. I fear that they’ll find an excuse to declare an emergency of some sort to justify the use of troops. But I know we can still win. Eighteen months ago, some of the anti-democracy machinations we are witnessing today would have seemed fanciful. We might have said, “No way that is going to happen” — but now, to be frank, we don’t have the luxury of hoping for the best. We have to fight for it. = | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = = | = = | = In spite of these valid fears, here is the honest truth: We have power. American history proves it. A group of revolutionaries took on the mightiest empire in the world and founded this nation. Americans fought to end slavery when its end once seemed impossible. Women fought for the right to vote. Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr., Diane Nash, John Lewis, and countless others understood the power of ordinary people to organize, to stand up, and to move this country forward. Progress happens because the people fight for it. That is what gives me hope now. But the fact that we have power is not, in and of itself, enough. We have to use it.= People sacrificed so much so that you and I could have the opportunity to express ourselves politically. We honor their work by using the power they fought to give us. I remain optimistic because I know what Americans are capable of when we understand our power and exercise it. = Eric H. Content warning: This message references violence.

Their cruelty is the point,
Peter.

ICE is still on a rampage across our country, and the detention centers
they run are fundamentally inhumane. They are sites of state-sanctioned
violence and neglect.

We are mourning deaths that never had to happen. Just recently, Edwin
Jovanny Lopez Cornejo died at Delaney Hall because he was denied basic
medical care — a direct result of an administration that treats immigrant
lives as disposable.

And Edwin isn’t the first. Renee Good. Alex Pretti. Dr. Linda Davis.
Lorenzo Salgado Araujo. Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero. Keith Porter Jr.

These are just some of the names of people who have had their lives taken
during encounters with ICE agents who continue to act without consequence.
And there are dozens more who have died in ICE custody that we know of.

Our Squad members are demanding accountability and change. Ilhan recently
visited the Whipple Federal Building to urge an overhaul of the
unsustainable, fatal ICE procedures exposed by the "Metro Surge" raids —
only to be met with stonewalling and minimal answers. Meanwhile, Ayanna
described her visit to Dilley ICE Detention Center as "harrowing and
horrific" — demanding the immediate closure of the facility.

We will not normalize this cruelty. We will not look away while Trump's
authoritarian regime carries out a campaign of terror against our
neighbors. We must condemn, resist, and reject every attempt to dehumanize
our immigrant communities.

We must abolish ICE. That’s the fight. And that’s our ask today.

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

body:
If you’re ready for change, please read this email.
---
| [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-hamilton-split?amount=20&refcode=em_20260810_8521_fr&refcode2=8521_22930333_F7m0Ui&akid=8521%2E22930333%2EF7m0Ui)
---
_Grateful. Humbled. Invigorated._
Derek, these are just a few words to describe how I’m feeling after winning my primary to become the official Democratic Senate nominee for the great state of Kansas.
I got into this race because I was fed up with watching politicians in Washington make decisions that harmed the people and communities I love. And you know what I’ve learned over several months on the campaign trail? A lot of others are fed up, too.
**People are ready for change. Ready for leaders who will put people over politics. Ready for a senator who will actually listen and bring people together to solve our problems. If you’re one of those people, Derek,** [**please consider making a $20 donation today — split between my campaign and the DNC — to help get my general election campaign off to the strongest possible start as one of our first General Election Founding Donors.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-hamilton-split?refcode=em_20260810_8521_fr&amount=20&refcode2=8521_22930333_F7m0Ui&akid=8521%2E22930333%2EF7m0Ui)
This might be my first foray into politics, but after more than three decades serving Kansas communities as a pastor, I believe I can be a better listener, a better bridge-builder and a better champion for Kansans than incumbent Sen. Roger Marshall.
**And with early polling showing us neck and neck, I am confident we can win this race. It’s time we restore common sense and decency to our government and address the serious problems that we as a nation are facing.**
I’m not naive. Kindness and compassion alone will not cure what ails us, and confidence alone will not win this race. Simply put, we are going to need a lot more people on this team and a lot more resources to keep up our incredible early momentum.
[**Roger Marshall has corporate PACs funding his campaign; I have this grassroots team. That’s why I am personally asking: Will you split a donation of $20 or more today between my campaign and the DNC to become a Founding Donor as we enter general election season in Kansas and beyond?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-hamilton-split?refcode=em_20260810_8521_fr&amount=20&refcode2=8521_22930333_F7m0Ui&akid=8521%2E22930333%2EF7m0Ui)

subject: Someone had to pay – and as union president, my head was on the chopping block.

body:
It’s easy to let yourself get beaten down by life. To let big corporations and the politicians they own in Washington make all the decisions – and just accept that that’s how things will always be. But that’s not me.
[](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/107293?refcode=em20260810-10773&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=10773%2E614464%2EcR-P1o)
In October 2021, I had been an employee of Kellogg’s for almost 18 years.
I had dropped out of college and gone to work for the company after my wife got pregnant. Life’s easy when all you gotta do is take care of yourself – but we needed diapers and health insurance for our growing family.
Working at Kellogg’s used to be a lifelong career. A good-paying job that let you become a homeowner, live decently, and hopefully retire some day.
But over the years, that changed. Workers were paid less. Cost of living adjustments weren’t keeping up anywhere near inflation. Retirement and health insurance plans were gutted. It just wasn’t right. They were making record profits – and doing it off the backs of workers.
**So in October 2021, we walked out. And as president of our local union, I led the strike.**
[](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/107293?refcode=em20260810-10773&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=10773%2E614464%2EcR-P1o)
Most of us had never walked a picket line. It was cold, but we were determined to hold our lines through the dead of the winter if we had to. We were a part of something bigger than ourselves. We were in a fight for the future of the American middle class.
After 11 weeks in the cold, we reached an agreement. More importantly, we saved 500 good-paying union jobs.
It was one of the proudest moments of my life.
[](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/107293?refcode=em20260810-10773&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=10773%2E614464%2EcR-P1o)
Following the strike, I was fired. Someone had to pay – and as union president, my head was on the chopping block.
It’s easy to let yourself get beaten down by life. To let big corporations and the politicians they own in Washington make all the decisions – and just accept that that’s how things will always be. But that’s not me.
Instead, I decided last year to run against one of the most corporate politicians – U.S. Senator Republican Deb Fischer – and we nearly won. I got 47% of the vote in one of the closest Senate races in the country.
**Now, I’m running again for the U.S. Senate – this time against billionaire Republican Pete Ricketts – and the first poll shows us virtually TIED: 46% to 45%.**
I am taking on a literal billionaire senator. We can finish what we started last year and flip Nebraska’s Senate seat for working class people, but I need grassroots donors like you to give now if we’re going to win this seat.
**[Please, will you contribute to my campaign for U.S. Senate and Heartland Patriots to help me defeat billionaire Republican Pete Ricketts here and flip Nebraska’s Senate seat?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/107293?refcode=em20260810-10773&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=10773%2E614464%2EcR-P1o)**

clean_body: It’s easy to let yourself get beaten down by life. To let big corporations and the politicians they own in Washington make all the decisions – and just accept that that’s how things will always be. But that’s not me. In October 2021, I had been an employee of Kellogg’s for almost 18 years. I had dropped out of college and gone to work for the company after my wife got pregnant. Life’s easy when all you gotta do is take care of yourself – but we needed diapers and health insurance for our growing family. Working at Kellogg’s used to be a lifelong career. A good-paying job that let you become a homeowner, live decently, and hopefully retire some day. But over the years, that changed. Workers were paid less. Cost of living adjustments weren’t keeping up anywhere near inflation. Retirement and health insurance plans were gutted. It just wasn’t right. They were making record profits – and doing it off the backs of workers. So in October 2021, we walked out. And as president of our local union, I led the strike. Most of us had never walked a picket line. It was cold, but we were determined to hold our lines through the dead of the winter if we had to. We were a part of something bigger than ourselves. We were in a fight for the future of the American middle class. After 11 weeks in the cold, we reached an agreement. More importantly, we saved 500 good-paying union jobs. It was one of the proudest moments of my life. Following the strike, I was fired. Someone had to pay – and as union president, my head was on the chopping block. It’s easy to let yourself get beaten down by life. To let big corporations and the politicians they own in Washington make all the decisions – and just accept that that’s how things will always be. But that’s not me. Instead, I decided last year to run against one of the most corporate politicians – U.S. Senator Republican Deb Fischer – and we nearly won. I got 47% of the vote in one of the closest Senate races in the country. Now, I’m running again for the U.S. Senate – this time against billionaire Republican Pete Ricketts – and the first poll shows us virtually TIED: 46% to 45%. I am taking on a literal billionaire senator. We can finish what we started last year and flip Nebraska’s Senate seat for working class people, but I need grassroots donors like you to give now if we’re going to win this seat. If you have stored your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation to Dan Osborn and Heartland Patriots will process instantly: I believe we can win this race and keep up the fight for the American middle class. clean_body: President Trump has a message for you, and we need your help to answer a dishonest attack before tomorrow. | Peter - President Trump has a message for you: President Trump: "She has what it takes" Thank you, President Trump. Your support and endorsement mean the world to me - especially right now. I won't sugarcoat it, Peter: my primary opponents are running dishonest attack ads twisting my work helping South Carolinians with disabilities find good jobs and get off government assistance. It's exactly the kind of conservative fighting I've built my career on, and exactly why President Trump endorsed me. Now more than ever, I need you to stand with me in the final hours before this Special Primary Election. Every dollar you give today goes straight into our Get-Out-The-Vote Fund — phone banks, canvassers, and volunteers working around the clock to counter these smears and turn out the voters who will decide this race tomorrow. I will earn South Carolinians' votes, and I promise to work hard every single day for South Carolina. But I can't out-hustle these attacks without you. , and encourage your friends, family, neighbors, and coworkers in South Carolina to vote in tomorrow's Special Election. To quote my brother, Lindsey, if you don't have a friend, make one and take them with you to vote! There’s a reason this story mattered to Charlie| | | |
---
| | | Patriot,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

Patriot, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story...

It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now.

So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together.

Young people face that pressure every single day.

They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is.

JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion.

He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back.

That's what _Communion_ is about...

And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now.

name: Aaron Ford
subject: Why I keep a stale candy bar in my office
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Committee to Elect Aaron Ford
body:
I got here because of food stamps, Medicaid and WIC — not despite them.
# [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=655%2E127862%2E4ibNru)
Listen — if you'd told me as a kid I'd grow up to run for governor, I would've laughed at you.
That wasn't in the cards for a kid like me. It never even crossed my mind.
My dad stocked shelves at Safeway. My mom worked odd jobs before she found her way into the postal service. We worked hard, and we still struggled. **I remember one night, all my brother and I had for dinner was a stale candy bar — a Skor bar, to be exact.**
[](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260810_2_ak.f3xeGo&amount=5&refcode=em20260810-651&t=3&akid=655%2E127862%2E4ibNru)I still keep one on my desk today. Not to eat it. Just so I never forget where I come from.
Programs like food stamps, Medicaid, and WIC kept my family standing when we needed it most. They're the reason I made it through school. Not despite the government investing in us — _because of it._
That's what's so infuriating about watching MAGA Gov. Joe Lombardo help gut those same programs. **He's siding with billionaire donors and special interests while Nevada families are struggling.**
Our government shouldn't exist to please corporations while working people barely scrape by. **I’m a living, breathing example of what can happen to someone when their government has their back.**
Those programs allowed me to go on to earn five degrees, teach math in a public school classroom, and become Nevada's first Black Attorney General. None of that happens without that crucial support.
As governor, that's exactly what I intend to do for Nevadans — _invest_ in them, the way this country once invested in me.
**[If you're with me, chip in $5 and help us keep building this campaign to move Nevada forward:](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260810_2_ak.f3xeGo&amount=5&refcode=em20260810-651&t=4&akid=655%2E127862%2E4ibNru)**

Thank you,
Aaron

Enough of leaders who pick fights, point fingers, and treat public service

elected to serve.

families to pay the price.

Here in Pennsylvania, we’ve shown there’s another way: Lowering costs,

safer, and getting stuff done.

# I started a show
### Tuesdays. Paid subscribers see it first.
| | | [Harry Dunn](https://substack.com/@harrydunn)
---
| Aug 10
---
| [](https://substack.com/@harrydunn)
---
Most of you signed up for the writing. I'm still doing that.
But I started something new, and I want to make sure you know it exists.
Every Tuesday I put out a show called Standing Our Ground. Ten minutes or so, me on camera. The stories that matters that week, the part of it I can speak to that most people can't, and one person who stood up when it cost them something.
Some things land differently when you can see somebody's face while they say them. That's why I started it.
[Paid subscribers get it on Tuesday here on Substack (free preview)](https://substack.com/redirect/126e0606-58e9-4f40-b284-f309bf95fe41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). It goes public on [my YouTube page](https://substack.com/redirect/fd8554f7-b74a-4fdb-901e-d8726df1f5ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the following Saturday.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/126e0606-58e9-4f40-b284-f309bf95fe41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
That's not a trick, it's just how I keep this funded without taking money from anyone who'd want something back for it. No donors, no party, nobody I have to run a draft past.
Paid also gets you Off Duty on Fridays -- the personal writing, no news hook, just where my head's at. And the monthly Q&A, where you ask and I answer live.
It is $80 a year. About seven bucks a month »
[Get 10% off for 3 months](https://substack.com/redirect/d8f80afe-4634-4318-93f2-848a0e83e4b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
If you're staying free, nothing changes and I mean that. The Good Trouble Report on Wednesdays, the daily posts, The 6th every month, the whole YouTube channel -- all still free, all still yours.
Either way, thanks for being here.
-- Harry
PS. [Monthly's $8 if that's easier.](https://substack.com/redirect/44970ab9-47db-49d5-b760-c7a0bed5fbca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

body:
With young, progressive leaders, we’re setting a precedent for what’s possible in American politics.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260809-2&t=1&akid=3851%2E587540%2EDeq6wR)
Peter,
What we’re building together is bigger than one election.
Yes, we’re fighting to elect bold, progressive leaders in this year’s midterms. But we’re also doing something much bigger: **we’re changing what’s possible in American politics.**
Every time one of our young candidates defeats a corporate-funded establishment Democrat, it sends a message that ripples far beyond a single district.
It tells the next generation of leaders that they don’t need mega donors or corporate PACs to run a winning campaign.
**It tells young progressives that their voices, their ideas, and their vision for the future belong at every level of government.**
And it proves that candidates who are willing to challenge the status quo can build winning campaigns rooted in their communities, not in corporate money.
That matters because people are watching.
Young organizers. Community advocates. Local leaders. First-time candidates who have spent years wondering whether someone like them could ever run for office _and win._
When they see grassroots campaigns succeed against the odds, they begin to believe they can do it, too.
That's how movements grow. One victory inspires another. One campaign encourages another young leader to step forward. One breakthrough changes what an entire generation believes is possible.
The precedent we set in these midterms won't stop on Election Day. It will shape who decides to run in 2028, who believes they have a chance, and what kind of Democratic Party we build for decades to come.
That's why we need _you._
You're not just helping elect one candidate or flip one seat. You're helping lay the groundwork for a generational revolution by inspiring a new generation of progressive leaders to step up, run for office, and prove that people-powered campaigns can win in every corner of this country.
**[So, Peter, will you make a contribution of $5 today to help us elect the leaders we deserve?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260809_2_precedent.sTlev4&refcode=em20260810-3851&amount=5&t=2&akid=3851%2E587540%2EDeq6wR)**

Thank you,
Leaders We Deserve

body:

I need to tell you something I don't talk about enough.
Outside of my office, a group of extremists gathered and screamed what translates to "Death to Krishnamoorthi" at the top of their lungs.
A crowd of people, in America, calling for my death.
I'm an immigrant. The son of people who came to this country with nothing because they believed it was a place where you could live freely, speak freely, and serve your community without fearing for your life. A place where disagreement didn't end in threats of violence.
Sadly, this is nothing new. I have faced this before.
A sitting Republican elected official also publicly tagged the Department of Homeland Security on social media to report me as a "foreign occupier" with an "unpronounceable name" and called for the mass deportation of Indians. I have been mocked, threatened, and told in a hundred different ways that someone like me doesn't belong in American public life.
And every single time, I have made the same choice.
Keep going.
Because the moment I stop — the moment I let the hatred win — is the moment I break faith with every family that came to this country believing it was worth fighting for. Including my own.
This is the America we are living in right now. Extremists feel emboldened to threaten, intimidate, and silence the people who are trying to do the work. Hatred has been given permission to operate in the open. The machinery of government is being used to make certain communities feel like they don't belong.
Equal Opportunity Now exists because we need leaders who have faced this kind of hatred and didn't flinch. Who know what it costs to keep going and choose to keep going anyway. Who will stand up — not just for themselves, but for every family that is being targeted, threatened, and told they don't belong.
Those leaders are out there. And they need our support right now.

They can scream all they want.
We are not slowing down.
— Raja Krishnamoorthi

White House officials framed the move as a pivot to , noting America's schedule remains more crowded than those of European and Asian peers. Lisa Murkowski and Susan Collins broke ranks to oppose the .
